column4: Head-On Crash on Old Mill Road
column5: While impaired, unlawfully and unintentionally caused the death of {V} in a collision on Old Mill Road.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, {D}'s Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside {HOOD} and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. The Corolla's driver, {V}, 34, a nurse driving home from a twelve-hour shift, died at the scene. {D}, a line cook at {REST}, had stayed after closing that night. A hospital blood test about ninety minutes after the crash and a second, State Crime Laboratory test about three hours after it disagree on whether {DL} was over the legal limit when the cars collided. {DL} says a deer came out of the tree line and {D.he} swerved.
column7: N.C. State Highway Patrol crash investigator
column8: {DL} was the driver of the Civic and remained at the scene.

column4: Church Treasurer Charged in Missing Building Fund
column5: As treasurer, embezzled $112,400 from {CHURCH}.
column6: For six years {D}, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of {CHURCH} in {HOOD}. When a new trustee asked for the building fund statements, $112,400 was gone, moved over three years in 41 checks and transfers to an account in the name of "DL Property Services." {DL} says Pastor {PASTOR} approved every payment as short-term loans to the contractor rebuilding the fellowship hall, and that the paperwork was handshakes. The pastor, now retired and in poor health, says no such arrangement existed.
column8: {DL} was the treasurer and the only signer on the account that received the money.

column4: Intruder in the Hallway on {STREET}
column5: Broke and entered the occupied dwelling of {V} at night with intent to commit larceny.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, {V} woke to a noise in a duplex on {STREET} in {HOOD} and saw a stranger in the hallway, lit only by a nightlight. The intruder ran out the back door, which had been pried open, taking a laptop, a wallet, and a bottle of prescription pain pills. Four days later {D} sold the laptop to a pawn shop a few miles away. {DL} says the laptop came from a man at a gas station who sold it for $80, and that {D.he} was home asleep that night.
column8: The stolen laptop was pawned under {DL}'s name four days after the burglary.

column4: Domestic Call on {STREET} Ends in Strangulation Charge
column5: Assaulted {V} and inflicted physical injury by strangulation.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, {V} called 911 from a bathroom in the house on {STREET} that {V.he} shared with {D}, saying {DL} had choked {V.him} in the kitchen. Deputies found red marks on {VL}'s neck and a broken skillet on the floor; {DL} had fresh scratches on the face and forearm. {DL} says {VL} came at {DL} with the skillet after a night of drinking and {D.he} grabbed {VL} to stop it. By trial, {V} says {V.he} had been drinking heavily and can't remember who started it.
column8: {DL} was in the house when deputies arrived; both parties named each other.

column4: Cocaine Found in Shared Apartment
column5: Possessed cocaine with intent to sell or deliver.
column6: On {DATE}, narcotics detectives executed a search warrant at a three-bedroom apartment on {STREET} in {HOOD}, leased to {D} and shared with two roommates. In a shoebox on the top shelf of the hall closet they found 31 knotted baggies of cocaine totaling 22.4 grams and $1,840 in cash; a digital scale was in a kitchen drawer. {DL} was the only person home. One roommate, {ALT}, who has a prior conviction for selling cocaine, moved out two days later. {DL}, a warehouse forklift operator, says the closet was shared and the box wasn't {D.hers}.
column8: {DL} held the lease and was the only person home when the warrant was executed.

column4: Caregiver Accused of Draining Client's Savings
column5: Knowingly exploited {V}, an older adult, by using {V.his} funds for {DL}'s own benefit through deception and undue influence.
column6: For two years {D}, a home health aide, cared for {V}, 91, a retired textile mill supervisor who lives alone in {HOOD}. Over fourteen months, $68,000 left {VL}'s savings: checks to {DL} written in {D.his} handwriting and signed by {VL}, a used car titled to {DL}, and cash withdrawals made with {VL}'s debit card. {VL}'s niece, who lives in Ohio, found the statements after {V.he} fell and was hospitalized. {DL} says {VL} insisted on every gift and called {DL} "the only family who shows up." {VL}, who has mild dementia but sometimes recalls things clearly, has told different people different things.
column8: {DL} wrote the checks, received the money, and holds title to the car bought with {VL}'s funds.

column4: Driver Shot in {LOT} Parking Lot
column5: Assaulted {V} with a handgun, with intent to kill, inflicting serious injury.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, after a near-collision on {STREET}, {V} followed {D}'s pickup into the parking lot of {LOT} in {HOOD}. {V} got out and walked to {DL}'s driver's door. {DL}, who has a concealed carry permit, fired twice through the open window, hitting {V} in the shoulder and abdomen. {V} survived after surgery. {DL} says {V} reached into the truck and grabbed {DL}'s collar; {V} says {V.he} only knocked on the door frame and yelled. A store camera caught most of it from sixty yards away.
column8: {DL} called 911, identified as the shooter, and remained at the scene.

column4: Six Families, Six Deposits, No Kitchens
column5: Obtained a $14,500 deposit from {V} by falsely representing that materials had been ordered for {V.his} kitchen remodel.
column6: Over five months, {D}, owner of {BIZ} in {HOOD}, took deposits from six homeowners for kitchen and bathroom remodels, $61,000 in all. None of the work was finished; three jobs never started. {V} paid $14,500 after {DL} told {VL} the cabinets were "already on order and arriving in three weeks." No cabinets were ever ordered. {DL} says the business collapsed when a supplier went under and {D.he} was robbing Peter to pay Paul to keep it alive, not stealing. The State charged each family's deposit as its own count; {VL}'s leads the indictment because of what {DL} said to get it.
column8: {DL} owned {BIZ} and personally sent the text to {V}.

column4: Business Partner Shot Dead at {LAKE} Cabin
column5: Killed {V} with a shotgun, with malice, premeditation, and deliberation.
column6: {D} and {V} owned {SHOP} together for eleven years. On {DATE}, during a cold snap, the two drove to {VL}'s cabin on {LAKE} to hunt ducks. At about {TIME}, {DL} called 911 to say the shotgun had gone off while {D.he} was unloading it on the porch and {VL} was dead. The medical examiner says the shot was fired from about four feet away. Three weeks earlier, {VL} had told a lawyer {V.he} wanted to force {DL} out of the business, and the company held a $500,000 life insurance policy on each partner payable to the other.
column8: {DL} was the only other person at the cabin and reported the shooting.

column4: Couple Tied Up in {HOOD} Home Invasion
column5: With another person, robbed {V} in {V.his} home while armed with a handgun.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, two masked people forced their way into the home of {V}, 67, and {V.his} spouse on {STREET} in {HOOD}, held them at gunpoint, zip-tied their wrists, and took a gun safe's contents, jewelry, and $3,000 in cash. Two weeks later police arrested {ALT}, who sold one of the stolen rifles. {ALT} agreed to testify in exchange for a reduced charge and named {D} as the partner who carried the handgun. {DL} says {ALT} is protecting the real accomplice.
column8: {DL} was named by the co-defendant, {ALT}, after {ALT.he} agreed to cooperate.

column4: Ex-Partner Cut During Visit Under Protective Order
column5: Assaulted {V} with a box cutter, a deadly weapon, inflicting serious injury, while a domestic violence protective order was in effect.
column6: {V} held a domestic violence protective order against {D}, the other parent of their eight-year-old, that barred contact except for exchanges arranged through a relative. On {DATE}, {DL} came to {VL}'s apartment on {STREET} unannounced at about {TIME} to pick up the child's medicine and school clothes. Minutes later {VL} called 911 with a deep cut across the forearm that took nineteen stitches and nerve repair. {VL} says {DL} pulled a box cutter. {DL} says {VL} grabbed the box cutter off the counter and {DL} was cut too trying to take it away.
column8: {DL} was present when officers arrived; both parties described a struggle over the box cutter.

column4: Rape Charge After Off-Campus Party
column5: Engaged in vaginal intercourse with {V}, who was physically helpless and mentally incapacitated by alcohol, when {DL} knew or should reasonably have known of that condition.
column6: On {DATE}, {V} and {D}, students at Hollis State University, were both at an off-campus party on {STREET}. Friends say {VL} drank heavily over several hours. At about {TIME}, {DL} and {VL} left together for {DL}'s apartment two blocks away. The next morning {VL} woke there with no memory after the party and went to the hospital, where a sexual assault examination was done. {DL} says {VL} was drunk but awake, talking, and an eager participant. {VL} says {V.he} could not have agreed to anything.
column8: {VL} woke in {DL}'s apartment; DNA confirmed intercourse with {DL}.

column4: Landlord Charged After Fire Guts Rental with Tenants Inside
column5: Willfully and maliciously burned the dwelling at {STREET}, occupied at the time by {V} and family.
column6: {D} owns six rental houses in {HOOD}. For four months {DL} had been trying to evict {V}, who withheld rent over a broken furnace and filed a complaint with the city housing inspector. At about {TIME} on {DATE}, fire broke out in the rental's back room while {V} and {V.his} two children slept. A smoke alarm woke them and all three escaped. The fire marshal found gasoline in the back room. {DL} says {D.he} was home asleep, and that the tenants were running a space heater on an extension cord because of the furnace.
column8: Investigators focused on {DL} based on the eviction dispute, the threatening text, the insurance increase, and a pickup resembling {D.his} on a neighbor's camera.

column4: Parent Charged in Deaths of Two Children
column5: Killed {KID1} and {KID2}, the defendant's children, with malice, premeditation, and deliberation.
column6: On the night of {DATE}, {D}, a teacher on leave four months after the family's third child was born, was alone with the children in their home in {HOOD} while {D.his} spouse worked an overnight shift at the hospital. Shortly after 2 a.m. a neighbor found {DL} in the backyard, soaked and shivering, saying "they're safe now." Inside, the two older children, {KID1}, 6, and {KID2}, 4, had died of asphyxia in their beds. The baby was unharmed. In the months since the birth, {DL} had been seen by three providers and had stopped sleeping. The State says {DL} chose a night alone. The defense says {DL} was in a postpartum psychosis and believed {D.he} was rescuing the children from something worse.
column8: {DL} was the only adult in the home.

column4: Deputy Found Dead in Snow After Party
column5: Killed {V} by striking {V.him} with a motor vehicle while impaired, with malice.
column6: During an ice storm on {DATE}, {D} drove {D.his} partner, {V}, a Hollis County sheriff's deputy, to a party at a fellow deputy's house on {STREET}, after the two had argued at a bar. At 6:15 a.m., {DL} and two friends found {VL} unconscious in a ditch at the edge of the yard; {VL} died at the hospital of a head injury and hypothermia. {DL}'s SUV had a broken passenger mirror. The State says {DL}, drunk and furious, clipped {VL} while making a fast U-turn and drove away. The defense says {VL} went inside, something happened there, and the deputies at that party steered the investigation toward {DL}.
column8: {DL} dropped {VL} off, and {DL}'s SUV had a broken mirror.

column4: Car Dealer Charged in Spouse's Shooting
column5: Killed {V}, the defendant's spouse, with a rifle, with malice, premeditation, and deliberation.
column6: {D} owns the biggest car dealership in Hollis County, founded by {D.his} grandparent. At 9:52 p.m. on {DATE}, {DL} called 911 to report finding {D.his} spouse, {V}, shot in the horse barn on the family's farm outside {HOOD}. {DL} said {D.he} had been at the house watching a game and then drove to check on an elderly parent. That afternoon, the dealership's bank had frozen its accounts over $1.2 million in customer down payments that never reached lenders. A video {VL} took of a sick horse at 8:31 p.m. captured {DL}'s voice in the barn.
column8: The barn video placed {DL} with {VL} minutes before the shooting.

column4: Parent Charged After Child Missing 19 Days
column5: Killed {KID}, age three, the defendant's child, with malice, premeditation, and deliberation.
column6: {KID}, three, was last seen at day care on {DATE}. For nineteen days {D} told family that {KID} was at the beach with a coworker's relative. When {DL}'s parent pressed and called the Sheriff's Office, {D.he} admitted {KID} was missing but said {KID} had been taken from a park. Five weeks later, {KID}'s remains were found in a storage tote in a creek bed four miles from the apartment. The medical examiner could not determine a cause of death. The State says {DL} drugged and suffocated {KID}. The defense says {KID} died of an accidental overdose of allergy medicine and {DL}, terrified, hid it.
column8: {DL} was the last adult with {KID} and gave false accounts.

column4: Teen Guarding Store Shoots Two After Hurricane
column5: Killed {V} with a rifle, with malice.
column6: Two nights after Hurricane {STORM} knocked out power across the county, {D}, a teenager, stood outside {D.his} uncle's hardware store on {STREET} with an AR-style rifle, saying {D.he} was protecting it from looters. At about {TIME} on {DATE}, {V} walked up, argued with {DL}, and grabbed for the rifle. {DL} fired three times, killing {VL}. As {DL} backed away, {VL}'s friend came at {DL} with a tire iron, and {D.he} fired again, wounding the friend. The State says {DL} brought a war rifle to a dark street and provoked the fight. The defense says {VL} tried to take the gun.
column8: {DL} called 911 and identified as the shooter.

column4: Pregnant Spouse Vanishes on Thanksgiving Morning
column5: Killed {V}, the defendant's spouse, with malice, premeditation, and deliberation.
column6: On Thanksgiving afternoon, {DATE}, {V}, seven months pregnant, was reported missing from the couple's home in {HOOD} by {D}, who said {D.he} had gone kayaking alone on {LAKE}, forty miles away, and came home to find {VL} gone and the dog in the yard. Three months later {VL}'s remains surfaced in a cove of {LAKE} about a mile from the boat ramp {DL} said {D.he} used. Investigators learned {DL} had a secret relationship with a coworker, had bought the kayak six days before without telling anyone, and was stopped at the Charlotte airport with a newly issued passport and $9,000 in cash the week the remains were found.
column8: The remains surfaced near {DL}'s only alibi location.

column4: Startup Founder Charged in Heart-Monitor Fraud
column5: In the offer and sale of securities, made untrue statements of material fact to {V} and other North Carolina investors.
column6: {D} founded {STARTUP}, a {CITY} company promising a ring that could detect heart attacks hours before they happened. North Carolina investors, including {V}, a retired dentist, put in $11 million. Former engineers say the ring never detected anything reliably, that demo results were pre-recorded, and that a letter of endorsement from a major hospital was written by {DL}. {DL} says the technology was close, that the chief engineer told {D.him} it worked, and that startups always sell the future.
column8: {DL} made the presentations and signed the offering documents.

column4: Teen Charged After Messages Urged Partner's Suicide
column5: By culpable negligence, through repeated messages encouraging {VL}'s suicide, unintentionally caused the death of {V.him}.
column6: {V}, 18, died by suicide in {HOOD} on {DATE}. Over the previous six weeks, {D}, {VL}'s partner of two years, sent hundreds of messages urging {V.him} to stop delaying and follow through, and was on a video call during the final hour without calling for help. Earlier in the relationship, {DL} had repeatedly urged {VL} to get treatment. The State says {DL}'s pressure was the cause, and that the failure to call for help was culpable negligence. The defense says {VL} had struggled for years, that words alone aren't a cause of death, and that {DL} was a teenager in crisis too.

column4: Jail Officer Charged in Inmate's Death
column5: Killed {V}, a detainee, by kneeling on {V.his} back and neck during a cell extraction, with malice.
column6: On {DATE}, {V}, 34, held in the Hollis County Detention Center on a probation violation, refused to leave a cell for a medical check during a mental health crisis. {D}, the sergeant leading a five-officer extraction team, pinned {VL} face-down and knelt across {V.his} upper back and neck for about six minutes after {V.he} was handcuffed. On jail video, {VL} says "I can't breathe" eleven times. {VL} stopped responding and died at the hospital. The defense says {VL} was violently resisting, had cocaine in {V.his} system, and died of an enlarged heart under stress.
column8: {DL} led the extraction team, on video.

column4: Council Candidate Charged With Faking Assault
column5: Willfully made a false report to the {CITY} Police Department that {DL} had been assaulted.
column6: Eleven days before a close {CITY} council election, {D} told police two masked people jumped {D.him} outside {D.his} campaign office at about {TIME} on {DATE}, spray-painting a slur on the window and punching {D.him}. The story went national. Police spent three weeks on it. Then two campaign volunteers said {DL} had paid them $1,800 to stage it, walked them through it the day before, and told them where the cameras were. {DL} says the attack was real and the volunteers turned on {D.him} to avoid charges.
column8: The volunteers named {DL} after the hardware store video identified them.

column4: Pharmacy Robbed of Painkillers at Gunpoint
column5: Robbed {V}, a pharmacist at {PHARM}, of oxycodone while armed with what appeared to be a handgun.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, a person in a hooded sweatshirt and surgical mask walked up to the pharmacy counter at {PHARM} in {HOOD}, lifted a black pistol from a jacket pocket, and told {V}, the pharmacist on duty, to empty the oxycodone drawer. {V} handed over 340 tablets. Police arrested {D}, a roofer with a pain-pill addiction, a week later after a tip; in {DL}'s truck they found a black CO2-powered BB pistol. {DL} admits the robbery and is pleading for the lesser charge: {DL} says it was a BB gun, not a firearm, and nobody's life was ever in danger.
column8: An anonymous tip, confirmed by the pharmacy video and the items in {DL}'s truck.

column4: Babysitter Charged After Infant's Brain Injury
column5: Intentionally inflicted serious physical injury on {INFANT}, a seven-month-old, by violent shaking.
column6: {D} ran a small licensed day care from {D.his} home in {HOOD}. On {DATE}, {DL} called 911 at about {TIME} to say seven-month-old {INFANT} had gone limp after falling from a changing table. At the hospital, doctors found bleeding beneath the skull, bleeding in both retinas, and brain swelling, and diagnosed abusive head trauma. {INFANT} survived with lasting developmental delays. {DL} says the baby rolled off the table while {D.he} reached for a diaper, and that the parents had noticed {INFANT} was fussy and vomiting the night before.
column8: {DL} was the only adult caring for {INFANT} when symptoms appeared.

column4: Bank Teller Charged With $38,000 Theft
column5: As an employee of {BANK}, embezzled $38,000 entrusted to {DL}.
column6: On {DATE}, a cash shipment in four sealed bags arrived at the {HOOD} branch of {BANK}. {D}, a teller, signed for it and placed it in the vault. At the end-of-day count, one bag, holding $38,000, was gone. Only {DL} and the assistant manager had vault access that afternoon, and the vault camera had been offline for nine days awaiting repair. Three weeks later, {DL} paid off a $14,000 car loan in cash. {DL} says the money came from a relative's settlement, and that the assistant manager had gambling debts.
column8: Vault badge records after the shipment arrived showed only {DL}.

column4: Cyclist Killed; Driver Says It Looked Like a Deer
column5: Knowing or having reason to know that the vehicle was involved in a crash causing death, failed to stop and remain at the scene.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, {V}, 29, was riding home on Rock Quarry Road outside {HOOD} when a car struck the bike from behind. {VL} died in the ditch. The driver didn't stop. Two days later, a body shop called police about a silver sedan with a shattered windshield brought in by {D}. {DL} admits driving that road that night and says {D.he} heard a bang, saw nothing in the mirror in the dark and rain, assumed it was a deer, and drove home. The question is whether {DL} knew, or had reason to know, a person was hit.
column8: A body shop owner reported {DL}'s damaged car.

column4: Fentanyl Pills Found in Rental Car on I-40
column5: Trafficked in opioids by possessing 28 grams or more of fentanyl pills.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, a trooper stopped a rental SUV for following too closely on I-40 near {HOOD}. {D} was driving; {ALT} was the passenger. A drug dog alerted, and in a duffel bag behind the passenger seat troopers found 1,100 blue pills, 121 grams, later confirmed as fentanyl. The SUV was rented in {DL}'s name. {DL} says {ALT} asked for a ride to Charlotte and brought the bag. {ALT} told the trooper the bag was {DL}'s and has since disappeared.
column8: {DL} was driving the rental SUV, rented in {D.his} name.

column4: One Punch Outside {CLUB} Leaves One Dead
column5: Unintentionally killed {V} by an unlawful assault, a single punch.
column6: At closing time on {DATE}, outside {CLUB} in {CITY}, {V}, 31, and {D} exchanged words after {VL} bumped {DL}'s friend in the line for rides. Video shows {VL} stepping toward {DL} and pointing in {D.his} face. {DL} threw a single punch. {VL} fell backward, struck the curb, and died two days later of a skull fracture and brain bleed. {DL} stayed, called 911, and held {VL}'s head still until paramedics came. The State says an unprovoked punch that kills is manslaughter. {DL} says {VL} was about to swing first.
column8: {DL} called 911 and stayed at the scene.

column4: Private Images Posted After Breakup
column5: Knowingly disclosed private intimate images of {V} without consent, with intent to cause harm.
column6: Three weeks after {V} ended a two-year relationship with {D}, private photos {VL} had shared only with {DL} appeared on a fake social media account tagged with {VL}'s employer and coworkers. The account was created from an IP address at {DL}'s apartment complex. {DL}, an IT help desk technician, says {D.his} old phone with the photos was stolen from {D.his} car two weeks earlier, that the complex's Wi-Fi is shared by 200 units, and that {D.he} would never do this.
column8: The images had been shared only with {DL}, and the account came from {D.his} apartment network.

column4: Felon Charged After Gun Found Under Car Seat
column5: Having been convicted of a felony, possessed a handgun.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, officers stopped a sedan for a broken taillight on {STREET} in {HOOD}. {D}, who has a felony drug conviction from nine years ago, was in the front passenger seat. The car belonged to the driver, {DL}'s cousin; a third person sat in the back. Under the front passenger seat, officers found a loaded pistol. The cousin and the backseat passenger both say they've never seen it. {DL} says the same. Nobody's fingerprints were on it.
column8: {DL} was seated directly above the pistol and has a felony conviction.

column4: Stolen Car Found Burned; Owner Charged With Fraud
column5: Presented a false statement in support of an insurance claim for the theft of {DL}'s vehicle.
column6: On {DATE}, {D} reported {D.his} pickup stolen from a restaurant parking lot in {HOOD} and filed a $41,000 insurance claim. Three days later the truck was found burned in a field six miles away. {DL} was three payments behind and owed more than the truck was worth. The fire was set with gasoline. Phone data puts {DL}'s phone a quarter mile from the field the night of the fire. {DL} says {D.he} drives that road to a client's house and that real thieves burn cars to destroy evidence.
column8: Flagged by the insurer's special investigations unit.

column4: Senior Charged After 'Don't Come Friday' Post
column5: Threatened to commit an act of mass violence on educational property.
column6: On {DATE}, {D}, a senior at {SCHOOL}, posted a short video to a private story seen by about 140 classmates: a photo of the school with the caption "don't come friday 💀" and a song with gunshot sound effects. Within an hour, parents flooded the school with calls; Friday attendance dropped by half. Deputies found no weapons in {DL}'s home, though {D.his} parent owns two hunting rifles kept in a locked safe. {DL} says it was a joke about a canceled pep rally and a big test, and that everyone who knows {D.him} knew that.
column8: {DL} posted from {D.his} own account and admitted it immediately.

column4: Ex-Partner Charged With Kidnapping After Five-Hour Drive
column5: Unlawfully restrained and removed {V} for the purpose of terrorizing {V.him}.
column6: On {DATE}, {D} showed up at {V}'s workplace parking lot in {HOOD} at shift change, six weeks after {V.he} ended their relationship. {VL} got into {DL}'s car. Five hours later {VL} jumped out at a gas station in Virginia and called 911, saying {DL} had locked the doors, taken {VL}'s phone, and threatened to drive them both off a bridge. {DL} says {VL} got in willingly to talk, that they argued for hours, and that {V.he} could have left at any of three stops.
column8: {VL} identified {DL}, and {D.he} was arrested at the scene.

column4: Neighbor Charged in Identity Theft of Retiree
column5: Knowingly used identifying information of {V} to open credit accounts and obtain goods.
column6: {V}, 79, lives in a duplex on {STREET} in {HOOD}, sharing a cluster mailbox with {D}, who lives next door and resells electronics online. Over four months, five credit cards were opened in {VL}'s name and used to buy $23,000 in laptops, gaming consoles, and phones, delivered to the cluster box or to a locker at a nearby store. {DL} sold more than thirty of those same models online during those months. {DL} says {D.he} buys inventory in bulk from liquidation sales, and that a mail carrier substitute that season was later fired for mail theft.
column8: Serial numbers of laptops bought with the fraudulent cards matched {DL}'s online sales.

column4: Homeowner Shoots Officer During Late-Night Raid
column5: Assaulted {OFF} with a firearm, with intent to kill, inflicting serious injury.
column6: At about {TIME} on {DATE}, a narcotics team executed a no-knock search warrant at a house on {STREET} in {HOOD}. The target, a suspected dealer, had moved out two months earlier; {D}, a truck driver home between runs, had moved in. Officers rammed the door. {DL}, woken in the dark, grabbed a pistol from the nightstand and fired as the first officer came down the hall, hitting {OFF} in the thigh. {DL} says {D.he} thought it was a home invasion. Officers say they announced "Police, search warrant" as they breached.
column8: {DL} was the shooter, inside the home.

column4: Friend Charged in Fentanyl Death
column5: Sold a pill containing fentanyl to {V}, whose ingestion of it caused {V.his} death.
column6: On {DATE}, {V}, 24, was found dead in {V.his} apartment in {HOOD}. Beside {VL} were an empty pill bag and a rolled-up dollar bill. Texts show {D}, a longtime friend and fellow server, sold {VL} two pills the night before for $40, which {DL} described as "perc 30s." The pills were counterfeit and contained fentanyl. {VL}'s toxicology also showed alcohol and a sedative prescribed to {V.him}. {DL} says {D.he} was passing along pills from {D.his} own supply, didn't know they had fentanyl, and that {VL}'s mix of drugs, not {DL}'s pill, caused the death.

column4: Alibi Witness Charged With Perjury
column5: Willfully and falsely testified under oath, in a material matter, that {ALT} was with {DL} on the night of a robbery.
column6: Last year {ALT} was tried for an armed robbery in {CITY}. {D}, {ALT}'s partner, testified under oath that the two were at home watching a movie all night. The jury hung. Before the retrial, a detective found security video from a casino two hours away showing {DL} at a slot machine at 10:40 p.m. that night, alone. {DL} is now charged with perjury. {DL} says {D.he} confused the night with another, testified honestly, and was coached by no one.

column4: Former Employee Charged With Extorting Executive
column5: Threatened to disclose {V}'s private affair unless paid $60,000.
column6: {D} worked for two years as executive assistant to {V}, a regional bank vice president in {CITY}, until being laid off in a restructuring. A gas can at {D.his} home holds a fuel mix that matches residue at two of the scenes. {DL} says {D.he} got to the fires first because {D.he} listens to the scanner and lives nearby.
column8: Radio logs showing {DL} on scene before dispatch, then phone records.

column4: Husband, 84, Charged After Shooting Wife With Dementia

column6: On {DATE}, {D}, 84, called 911 from the farmhouse in {HOOD} where he had lived with his wife, {V}, for sixty-one years. "I've shot my wife," he told the dispatcher. "I'll be on the porch." {VL}, 81, had advanced Alzheimer's. She no longer knew him, screamed through the nights, and had been refused by two memory care facilities after striking aides. Their savings were gone. {DL} told deputies that years earlier, when she was first diagnosed, she made him promise he would never let her "end up like that." He wrote a note, laid out his best suit, and shot her once while she slept. He had intended to shoot himself afterward but couldn't. The district attorney charged first-degree murder, saying the law doesn't allow anyone to decide another person's life is not worth living.

column4: Barn Explosion Kills Teen Helper at Illegal Still
column5: Unlawfully caused the death of {V}, age 17, by culpable negligence in operating a propane-fired liquor still in an enclosed barn.
column6: On {DATE}, an explosion blew the roof off a tobacco barn on {D}'s property in {HOOD} and started a fire that spread to a neighbor's barn. Inside was a 300-gallon copper still fired by propane, and {V}, 17, a neighbor's son {DL} paid $50 a night to watch the fire. {VL} died of burns two days later. Investigators found two propane tanks connected with garden hose and duct tape, no ventilation, and alcohol vapor that had collected under the barn roof. {DL} has run the still for years and sold to bootleggers in three counties. {DL} says the boy was told never to light a cigarette in the barn and must have.
column8: The fire and the still on {DL}'s land.

column4: After the Hurricane, a 'Relief Coordinator' Took Their Money
column5: Obtained more than $100,000 from homeowners in {HOOD} by falsely representing himself as a licensed contractor approved by FEMA to repair storm damage.
column6: Two weeks after a hurricane flooded {HOOD} and tore roofs off half the houses in the county, {D} arrived in a truck with a magnetic sign reading "FEMA Approved Disaster Recovery." Going door to door with a clipboard, {D.he} collected deposits from 31 families, mostly elderly, for roof and drywall work, and helped some fill out assistance applications, using their information to file six claims of {D.his} own. {V}, 77, gave {D.him} $14,000, nearly all of her insurance check. Almost no work was done. {D.His} contractor license was a photocopy of someone else's with the name changed. On {DATE}, {DL} was arrested in South Carolina, doing the same thing after another storm.
column8: Complaints to the attorney general's consumer protection line.

column4: Nursing Home Resident Dies of Untreated Sores
column5: Unlawfully caused the death of {V}, a resident, by culpable negligence in failing to provide care for pressure wounds over six weeks.
column6: On {DATE}, {V}, 88, a resident of a nursing home in {HOOD}, died of sepsis from pressure wounds so deep they exposed bone. She couldn't move on her own. State inspectors found the facility had run nights with one nursing assistant for 42 residents for months. The chart showed {VL} turned every two hours, with initials from assistants; one of them testifies that the assistants were never on that hall and never signed. {D}, the director of nursing, filled in the entries, the State says, to pass an inspection. {DL} says {D.he} begged the owners for staff in writing, and that the chart entries were "catching up" on care {D.he} believed had been given.
column8: A state inspection after {VL}'s family complained.

column4: 'Polite Bandit' Hits Fourth Bank With a Handwritten Note
column5: Took $3,140 from a teller at the First Coastal Bank branch in {HOOD} by passing a note threatening violence.
column6: Over five weeks, four bank branches in and around {HOOD} were robbed the same way: a man in a ballcap and reading glasses waited in line, slid a note across the counter reading "I have a gun. Give me the money in your drawer. No dye packs. Thank you," and walked out. On {DATE}, the fourth teller, {V}, saw him put his hand in his jacket pocket. A dye pack exploded in the bag outside. A witness photographed a red-stained man getting into a gold Buick. {D}, a roofer out of work after a back injury, owns a gold Buick, and red-stained bills were found in a trash can at {D.his} motel. {DL} admits the last robbery but says {D.he} had nothing to do with the first three.
column8: A witness's photo of the gold Buick and partial tag.

column4: Driver Claiming 'Sovereign' Status Drags Deputy at Traffic Stop
column5: Assaulted Deputy {OFFICER}, a law enforcement officer performing official duties, by driving off while the deputy's arm was caught in the car window, inflicting physical injury.
column6: On {DATE}, a deputy stopped {D} on {STREET} in {HOOD} for driving with a homemade license plate reading "PRIVATE TRAVELER - NOT FOR HIRE." {DL}'s license had been revoked for two years. {DL} refused to give a name, read from a laminated card claiming {D.he} was "not a person under the jurisdiction of the corporate State of North Carolina," and filmed the stop on {D.his} phone. When the deputy reached in to take the keys, {DL} rolled up the window on the deputy's arm and drove off, dragging the deputy twenty feet. {DL} was arrested at home later that day. {DL} has filed forty pages of handwritten motions claiming the court has no authority over {D.him}, and has clashed with appointed counsel over every filing.
column8: {DL} was identified from the vehicle and {D.his} own posted video.

column4: Hunter Kills Man Walking His Dog, Says He Thought It Was a Deer
column5: Unlawfully and unintentionally killed {V} by culpable negligence in firing a rifle at an unidentified target near a public trail.
column6: At dusk on {DATE}, {V}, 58, was walking a dog on a county greenway in {HOOD} when a single rifle shot hit {V.him} in the chest from 140 yards. {D}, hunting from a tree stand on posted county land that borders the trail, said {D.he} saw brown movement through the brush and thought it was a deer. {VL} was wearing a tan jacket. It was 23 minutes after legal shooting time ended. {DL} called 911 eleven minutes after the shot; investigators say the leash had been moved and the body turned. {DL} says {D.he} was trying to help.
column8: {DL} called 911 and stayed at the scene.

column4: 'Doctor' at Wellness Clinic Had No Medical License
column5: Assaulted {V} with a deadly weapon, a syringe of an unapproved substance, inflicting serious injury, by injecting her without valid consent obtained by fraud.
column6: For two years, {D} ran a "regenerative wellness" clinic in {HOOD}, wearing a white coat embroidered "Dr. {DL}" and offering IV vitamin drips and "stem cell" injections for joint pain at $4,000 a course. She had no medical degree; the diploma on the wall was from a school that doesn't exist, and the license number belonged to a retired Asheville pediatrician. On {DATE}, {V} was hospitalized with a severe infection in both knees after injections; {VIC2} was treated for sepsis a week later. Lab testing found the vials contained unsterile cord blood product from an overseas website. {DL} says she held a naturopathic certificate, never claimed to be a medical doctor, and that patients signed consent forms.
column8: Hospital reports to the health department.

column4: Local 'War Hero' Never Served, Records Show
column5: Obtained more than $100,000 in donations to a veterans' charity by falsely representing himself as a decorated combat veteran and the charity as a registered nonprofit.
column6: For six years, {D} spoke at Veterans Day events across {HOOD} in a uniform with a Bronze Star and a Purple Heart, telling of a firefight in Fallujah. {D.His} charity, Hometown Heroes Fund, raised $340,000 for veterans' housing and memorials. On {DATE}, a reporter's records request revealed that {DL} had never served in the military. The charity was never registered with the Secretary of State and had built one wheelchair ramp. Bank records show $61,000 went to a bass boat, a timeshare, and cash. {V}, whose son was killed in Afghanistan, paid $8,000 for a memorial bench in her son's name; it was never built. {DL} says {D.he} exaggerated but that the charity did real good.

column4: Wrong-Way Driver Kills Mother and Daughter on I-95
column5: Unlawfully and with malice killed {V} by driving while impaired the wrong way on Interstate 95, with three prior impaired driving convictions.
column6: At 1:52 a.m. on {DATE}, 911 operators took eleven calls about a pickup driving south in the northbound lanes of Interstate 95 near the {HOOD} exit. Four minutes later it hit {V}'s sedan head-on at a combined speed of about 130 mph. {VL} and her daughter, {KID}, 9, died at the scene. {D} survived with a broken pelvis. {D.His} blood alcohol was 0.25 at the hospital. {D.His} license had been revoked after {D.his} third impaired driving conviction, and a court had ordered an ignition interlock device; the pickup belonged to a friend and had none. Because of {D.his} prior convictions and the circumstances, the district attorney charged second-degree murder, which requires malice.
column8: {DL} was the driver, found in the pickup.

column4: Man Electrocuted Stealing Copper From Substation; Partner Charged
column5: Took and carried away copper grounding wire worth $2,800 from a Tidewater Power & Light substation, intending to permanently deprive the owner of it.
column6: Just after midnight on {DATE}, {D} and {V} cut through the fence of a power substation on the edge of {HOOD} with bolt cutters to steal copper grounding wire. {DL}, who had worked as an electrician's helper, told {VL} which wires were "dead." One wasn't. {VL} was electrocuted when he cut a cable connected to an energized transformer. The arc flash knocked out power to 4,000 homes, including a nursing home on oxygen machines. {DL} dragged {VL} to the truck, drove him to the hospital, and left before police arrived. Investigators found 300 pounds of copper in the truck bed and {DL}'s fingerprints on the bolt cutters. {DL} admits the theft but says {VL} chose to come and chose the wire.
column8: The truck seen leaving the hospital, and prints on the bolt cutters.

column4: Parent App Video Shows Daycare Teacher Striking Toddlers
column5: Intentionally inflicted serious physical injury on {KID}, age 2, a child in her care, by throwing him into a crib, fracturing his collarbone.
column6: On {DATE}, a mother checking the livestream app of a daycare in {HOOD} watched her son's teacher, {D}, throw him into a crib during nap time. She called police from her desk. Investigators reviewed three weeks of saved video from the toddler room: {DL} slapping a girl and pulling her hair, holding a blanket over a crying baby's face for eleven seconds, and, on three days, turning the camera toward the wall. The boy, {KID}, had a broken collarbone. {DL} had worked with the toddlers for eight months with no complaints. {DL} says she was handling eight toddlers alone, double what state ratios allow, and lost control on one bad day.
column8: A parent watching the daycare's livestream app.

column4: Audit: $214,000 Missing From Sheriff's Seized Cash Account
column5: While sheriff, embezzled $214,000 in seized drug money held in trust in the Sheriff's Office evidence account.
column6: A State Auditor's review of the Sheriff's Office found $214,000 missing from the account where cash seized in drug cases is held until the court orders it forfeited. On {DATE}, the former sheriff, {D}, who served four terms before losing the last election, was indicted. Bank records show cash withdrawals that line up with a down payment on a mountain cabin and campaign mailers. The evidence clerk, a 19-year employee, told auditors the sheriff ordered her to write "returned to owner" next to cases where no owner ever came. When she hesitated, she says, the sheriff told her, "You can find another job, or you can find a lawyer." {DL} says the money was spent on drug investigations and confidential informants, as sheriffs are allowed, and the records were poorly kept.

column4: Man Lured by Fake Dating Profile, Robbed and Held for Hours
column5: Unlawfully confined and restrained {V} for the purpose of committing robbery, and did not release him in a safe place.
column6: On {DATE}, {V}, 31, drove to an apartment complex in {HOOD} to meet a woman he'd been messaging on a dating app for two weeks. When he got out of his car, two men put a gun to his head, forced him into the back seat, and drove him to three ATMs over four hours, then left him zip-tied in a field off a dirt road. The profile used photos stolen from a model's Instagram. The State says {D} ran the profile, wrote the messages, and planned the meeting place. {DL}'s phone sent the last message, "I'm outside, come up," and the two men are {D.his} brother and cousin. {DL} says the brother used {D.his} phone and {D.he} never knew what they planned.
column8: Dating app records and the brother's car on ATM video.

column4: $74,000 in Bingo Money Missing From Veterans' Post
column5: As quartermaster of {POST}, embezzled $74,000 in bingo proceeds entrusted to {D.him} for the post.
column6: For six years {D} was the elected quartermaster of {POST} in {HOOD}, which runs bingo every Thursday night. The quartermaster counts the cash box with one other member, signs the count sheet, and takes the money to the bank on Friday. When state bingo regulators audited the post on {DATE}, they found the count sheets showed $212,000 over three years, but the post's account received $138,000. {V}, the post commander, says {DL} always insisted on making the deposits alone. {DL} says the missing money went to cash prizes and hall repairs that were never written down, and that the post's books were a mess long before {D.he} took over.
column8: {DL} signed every count sheet and made every deposit.

column4: Fire Destroys Century-Old Feed Store
column5: Wantonly and willfully set fire to and burned {STORE}, a store building in {HOOD}.
column6: {STORE} had been in {D}'s family for three generations. By {DATE} it was four months behind on its loan, and the bank had sent a foreclosure notice. At 2:15 a.m. that night a passing deputy saw flames in the back of the building. It burned to the ground. The state fire investigator found burn patterns on the floor in three separate places and traces of gasoline in two of them. Nine days later {DL} filed a $480,000 claim, having raised the policy's coverage four months earlier. {DL} says {D.he} was home asleep, that an old wiring problem started the fire, and that {D.he} raised the coverage because the bank required it.
column8: Motive, the policy change, and phone location records.

column4: Fight at Boat Ramp Leaves Fisherman With Fractured Skull
column5: Assaulted {V} with a deadly weapon, a wooden boat paddle, inflicting serious injury.
column6: On the morning of {DATE}, at the public boat landing on the river in {HOOD}, {D} and {V} argued over who had been waiting longer for the ramp. Witnesses agree {VL} walked down the dock toward {DL}'s boat shouting. What happened next is disputed. {DL} says {VL} reached for a filleting knife on {D.his} belt and {D.he} swung a wooden paddle once to keep {VL} back. {VL} fell, struck the dock cleat, and suffered a fractured skull. Deputies found a sheathed knife on {VL}'s belt. A witness says {VL}'s hands were empty and at {V.his} sides.
column8: {DL} stayed at the landing and told deputies {D.he} swung the paddle.

column4: Nurse Charged With Stealing Fentanyl Meant for Patients
column5: Obtained fentanyl, a Schedule II controlled substance, by fraud, deceit, and misrepresentation, by documenting doses as given or wasted that were not.
column6: {D} worked nights as a surgical recovery nurse at Hollis Regional Medical Center. The hospital's automated dispensing records showed {DL} withdrew fentanyl at three times the rate of other nurses on the unit, and recorded 212 partial doses as "wasted" over four months, often without a second nurse's witness signature. On {DATE}, a pharmacist tested a returned syringe {DL} had logged as fentanyl and found saline. A search of {DL}'s locker found two empty vials. {DL} says the unit was short-staffed, that nurses routinely skipped the witness step, and that someone else could have used {D.his} login.
column8: Dispensing records under {DL}'s login and the tested syringe.

column4: Store Clerk Shoots Armed Robber
column5: Took $612 from the person and presence of {V}, a clerk at {SHOP}, by the use of a handgun, whereby {V.his} life was threatened.
column6: Just after 11 p.m. on {DATE}, two people in ski masks walked into {SHOP} on {STREET} in {HOOD}. One pointed a black handgun at {V}, the clerk, and demanded the register. {V} handed over $612, then pulled a pistol from under the counter and fired twice as the two ran out. A trail of blood led across the lot. Forty minutes later {D} arrived at the emergency room with a gunshot wound to the shoulder, saying {D.he} had been shot during a drive-by. DNA from the blood trail matched {DL}. {DL}'s friend {ALT} was arrested the next week and agreed to testify. {DL} says {D.he} was shot walking past the store and ran because {D.he} panicked.
column8: DNA from the blood trail, the ER visit, and {ALT}'s statement.

column4: Out-of-State Owner Finds Her Land Sold Without Her
column5: Obtained $62,000 from {BUYER} by falsely representing that {D.he} had authority to sell a waterfront lot in {HOOD} owned by {V}.
column6: {V}, who lives in Ohio, inherited a vacant waterfront lot in {HOOD} and visited it once a year. On {DATE}, {V.he} drove down and found a house foundation being poured on it. The Register of Deeds showed a deed, signed in {V.his} name and notarized, transferring the lot to {BUYER} for $62,000. The sale proceeds went to an account opened by {D}, who had mowed the lot for {V} years earlier and once received a copy of {V.his} driver's license to pay a tax bill. The notary stamp belonged to a notary who died two years before the deed's date. {DL} says {D.he} was hired by a man named "Ray" to handle the paperwork and passed the money on to him.

column4: Homeowner Points Shotgun at Teens on Halloween
column5: Assaulted {V}, age 15, by pointing a shotgun at {V.him}.
column6: On Halloween night, {DATE}, a group of teenagers walked up {D}'s driveway in {HOOD}. {D}'s house had been egged on Halloween the two previous years. {DL} came out onto the porch with a pump shotgun. {V}, 15, says {DL} pointed it at {V.his} chest and said, "Next one of you on my porch gets buried." A neighbor's doorbell camera recorded the audio and part of the porch. {DL} says the shotgun was unloaded, that {D.he} held it pointed at the ground, and that {D.he} only wanted to scare off kids who had come to vandalize {D.his} house.

column4: Farmer Charged With DWI on Tractor
column5: Drove a vehicle, a farm tractor, on Highway 17 while under the influence of an impairing substance and with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.
column6: At 6:10 p.m. on {DATE}, two drivers on Highway 17 near {HOOD} swerved into the ditch to avoid a farm tractor crossing the center line. {TROOPER} stopped the tractor a mile on. {D} was driving it home from a friend's barbecue. The trooper smelled alcohol and saw red, glassy eyes; {DL} swayed on the clean-up walk test and refused the others. {D.His} breath test at the station, an hour and forty minutes later, was 0.09. {DL} says a tractor on a farm road isn't the same as a car, that {D.he} had two beers, and that the steering on the old tractor pulls left.

column4: Pill Press Seized in Rented Garage; 4,000 Counterfeit Pills Found
column5: Trafficked in opioids by manufacturing and possessing 28 grams or more of a mixture containing fentanyl.
column6: After three overdoses in {HOOD} in one week, all from blue pills stamped "M 30," detectives traced purchases to a house on {STREET} that {D} rented. On {DATE}, deputies executed a search warrant. In the detached garage they found a tabletop pill press, blue dye, binder powder, a digital scale, and two bags holding 4,000 pressed pills weighing 412 grams; lab testing found fentanyl in the mixture. {DL}'s fingerprints were on the press and the scale. {DL} says {D.his} roommate ran the garage, that {D.he} touched the press only to move it, and that the warrant's informant was unreliable.
column8: A controlled buy at the house and the lease in {DL}'s name.

column4: Woman's Body Found in Home Months After Death; Pension Kept Coming
column5: Failed to notify law enforcement of the death of {V}, with the intent to conceal the death.
column6: {V}, 84, a retired schoolteacher, lived with {V.his} adult child, {D}, in {HOOD}. When a neighbor hadn't seen {VF} in months, deputies made a welfare check on {DATE}. They found {VF}'s remains in a locked back bedroom. The medical examiner estimated death about eight months earlier, from heart disease, with no sign of injury. In those eight months, $26,400 in {VF}'s state teacher pension had been deposited and spent from a joint account, and an annual verification form, due in the spring, was signed with {VF}'s name. {DL} says {D.he} froze when {D.his} mother died, couldn't face it, and used the money to keep the house.

column4: Parent Takes Child to Florida in Violation of Custody Order
column5: Transported {KID}, age 7, outside North Carolina with the intent to violate a custody order of the Hollis County District Court awarding primary custody to {V}.
column6: Under a custody order entered eight months earlier, {V} had primary custody of their child, {KID}, 7, and {D} had every other weekend. On Friday, {DATE}, {DL} picked {KID} up for a weekend visit and did not return Sunday. {DL}'s phone was off. On Tuesday, police in Daytona Beach found the two at a motel after the Amber Alert. {DL} had withdrawn $3,000, enrolled {KID} in no school, and told the motel clerk they were "moving down for good." {DL} says it was a spur-of-the-moment beach trip, that {D.he} meant to come back, and that {D.he} turned the phone off because {V} kept sending threatening messages.

column4: Brawl After Rivalry Game Spills Into Parking Lot
column5: Willfully engaged in a riot, a public disturbance involving an assemblage of three or more persons, at {SCHOOL} stadium in {HOOD}.
column6: After a last-second loss in the rivalry game at {SCHOOL} on {DATE}, an argument between fans near the visitors' gate grew into a fight involving more than twenty people. {D}, a parent of one of the home team's players, was filmed by several phones swinging a metal folding chair. One swing struck {V}, a visiting fan, across the back, cracking two ribs. {DL} says {V} and three others had cornered {D.his} teenage son by the fence, and {D.he} grabbed the nearest thing to get them off him.
column8: Phone videos posted online, and {DL}'s jersey with {D.his} son's number.

column4: Street Race on Industrial Boulevard Kills Driver
column5: Unlawfully and unintentionally killed {V} by culpable negligence, racing another vehicle at more than 100 mph on Industrial Boulevard.
column6: Shortly after midnight on {DATE}, two cars lined up at a light on Industrial Boulevard in {HOOD}, where a crowd gathers on weekends to watch street races. When the light changed, both accelerated. A quarter mile on, {D}'s Mustang, going about 104 mph, struck {V}'s car as it pulled out of a warehouse lot after a night shift. {VL} died at the scene. The other racing car drove off. {DL} stayed, called 911, and tried CPR. {DL} says {D.he} wasn't racing, just accelerating hard, and that {VL} pulled out without looking.

column4: Felon Charged With Rifle at Hunting Camp
column5: Having been previously convicted of a felony, possessed a firearm, a .30-06 bolt-action rifle.
column6: On the opening day of deer season, {DATE}, a wildlife officer checked licenses at a hunting camp in the woods outside {HOOD}. {D}, convicted of felony breaking or entering fourteen years earlier, was sitting in {D.his} pickup with a .30-06 rifle in a case on the back seat and a fresh-killed doe in the truck bed. {DL} says the rifle belongs to {D.his} uncle, who shot the deer and asked {DL} to drive it and the rifle back to camp, and that {D.he} never handled the gun. The uncle confirms it. A box of .30-06 shells in the truck's console had {DL}'s fingerprint.

column4: Parent Charged With Cyberstalking Youth Baseball Coach
column5: Electronically communicated with {V} repeatedly from anonymous accounts for the purpose of abusing, annoying, threatening, and harassing {V.him}.
column6: {V} volunteers as head coach of a 12-and-under travel baseball team in {HOOD}. After benching several players for missing practice, {VL} began receiving messages from anonymous accounts: dozens over three weeks, insulting {V.his} coaching, posting {V.his} home address, and on {DATE} writing, "Coach better watch the parking lot after practice." A subpoena to the platform traced two of the accounts to an IP address at {D}'s house. {DL}'s child was one of the benched players. {DL} says {D.his} teenage nephew stayed at the house that month and used the home internet.
column8: Subscriber records for two of the accounts.

column4: Pharmacy Burglarized Overnight; Oxycodone Taken
column5: Broke and entered {PHARM}, a building in {HOOD}, with the intent to commit larceny therein.
column6: At 3:20 a.m. on {DATE}, the alarm at {PHARM} in {HOOD} went off. Deputies found the back door pried open and the Schedule II safe emptied of about 900 oxycodone and hydrocodone tablets. A latex glove dropped by the door held DNA matching {D}, whose profile was in the state database from a prior conviction. A muddy shoe print on the counter matched the tread of work boots seized from {DL}'s truck. {V}, the pharmacist-owner, says the safe's code was known only to staff, but the safe had been left unlocked that night. {DL}, who had roofed the pharmacy three months earlier, says the glove must have been left during that job.
column8: A DNA database match from the glove.

column4: Three Horses Found Starving in Muddy Pasture
column5: Intentionally deprived three horses of necessary sustenance, causing unjustifiable pain and suffering.
column6: A neighbor photographed three horses on {D}'s property outside {HOOD} for six weeks as they grew thinner, standing in a muddy pasture with no hay and a dry water trough. On {DATE}, animal control seized them. A veterinarian scored all three a 1 on the 9-point body condition scale, the lowest possible; one had to be euthanized. {DL} says {D.he} was in the hospital for three weeks of that time, that {D.he} paid a farmhand to feed them, and that the farmhand quit without telling {D.him}.
column8: {DL} owns the property and the horses.

column4: Grocery Store Fall Claim Was Staged, Insurer Says
column5: Presented a claim to {INSURER} for $85,000 knowing it contained false information that {D.he} was injured in an accidental fall at {GROCER}.
column6: On {DATE}, {D} fell in aisle seven at {GROCER} in {HOOD} and was taken to the emergency room complaining of back pain. {DL}'s lawyer sent a demand for $85,000, and the store's insurer paid a $6,500 advance for medical bills. The insurer's investigator then reviewed the store camera: thirty seconds before the fall, a person in {DL}'s clothing takes a bottle of cooking oil from the shelf, pours some on the floor, and puts the bottle back. The investigator also found two earlier fall claims by {DL} at other stores. {DL} says the camera angle is misleading, that {D.he} was reaching for the bottle when it leaked, and that {D.his} back injury is real.

column4: Woman Forced Into Car at Gas Station, Found Hours Later
column5: Unlawfully confined, restrained, and removed {V} from one place to another without consent for the purpose of terrorizing {V.him}, and did not release {V.him} in a safe place.
column6: At 9:40 p.m. on {DATE}, a gas station camera on {STREET} in {HOOD} recorded {D} grabbing {V}, {D.his} ex-girlfriend, by the arm at pump four and pushing her into the passenger seat of his car. Four hours later {V} was found by a deputy walking along a dark rural road twelve miles away, with a swollen eye and no phone. She says {DL} drove her around, screaming that she had ruined his life, hit her once, and left her on the road. {DL} says {V} got in willingly to talk, that they argued, and that she asked to be let out.

column4: Vacation Rental Burglarized; Owner's Doorbell Camera Catches Entry
column5: Broke and entered at night the dwelling house of {V} in {HOOD}, with the intent to commit larceny therein.
column6: {V} owns a beach house in {HOOD} that is rented weekly in season and sits empty in winter. At 11:52 p.m. on {DATE}, {V.his} doorbell camera recorded a person in a dark jacket opening the side door with a key-shaped object and going inside. Two televisions, a laptop, and jewelry were taken. {D}, whose company cleaned the house between rentals, had a key code to the lockbox. Two days later the laptop was sold at a pawn shop under {DL}'s name. {DL} says {D.he} bought the laptop from a stranger at a flea market and never went to the house that night.
column8: The pawn shop record and the lockbox code.

column4: Tax Preparer Charged With Using Clients' Identities
column5: Knowingly obtained and used the Social Security number and date of birth of {V}, a client, without consent, to open credit accounts in {V.his} name with the intent to fraudulently represent that {D.he} was {V}.
column6: {D} ran a storefront tax preparation office in {HOOD}. In {DATE}'s credit report, {V}, 79, a client for six years, found three credit cards {V.he} never applied for, with $7,800 in charges at electronics stores. A second client, {CLIENT2}, found a similar account. All the applications used the clients' Social Security numbers and dates of birth exactly as they appeared on the returns {DL} prepared, and listed a mailing address at a post office box rented by {DL}. {DL} says a former employee had access to every client file, and that the post office box was the office's business box.
column8: The post office box on every application.

column4: Payroll Bag Snatched at Poultry Plant
column5: Took $9,200 in cash from the person and presence of {V} by violence and putting {V.him} in fear.
column6: Every other Friday, {V}, an office manager at a poultry processing plant in {HOOD}, carried a bag of cash for workers who were paid in cash. On {DATE}, as {V} walked from the bank to the plant gate, someone in a hooded sweatshirt ran up, shoved {V.him} to the pavement, and grabbed the $9,200 bag. {V} broke {V.his} wrist in the fall. {D}, fired from the plant two months earlier, was identified from the gate camera by a supervisor. {DL} had paid off a $6,000 car loan in cash the next week. {DL} says {D.he} won the money gambling and was not at the plant that day.
column8: A supervisor's identification from gate video.

column4: Toddler Revived With Narcan After Swallowing Fentanyl
column5: Being the parent of {KID}, age two, created a substantial risk of physical injury to the child other than by accidental means, by leaving fentanyl pills within the child's reach.
column6: On {DATE}, {D} called 911 from {D.his} apartment in {HOOD}: {D.his} two-year-old, {KID}, was limp and barely breathing. Paramedics gave three doses of naloxone and {KID} recovered after two days in the pediatric unit; the hospital's urine screen was positive for fentanyl. Deputies found four blue pills on the nightstand beside the bed where {KID} napped, and a pill bottle with no label in a drawer. {DL} says the pills belonged to a houseguest who had stayed the night before, and that {D.he} didn't know they were there.

column4: DMV Examiner Assaulted Over Failed Road Test
column5: Assaulted {V}, a driver license examiner of the North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles, while {V.he} was discharging {V.his} official duties, by grabbing {V.him} by the collar and shoving {V.him} against a wall.
column6: On {DATE}, {D} failed the road test at the {HOOD} driver license office for the third time. Back inside, {DL} threw the score clipboard at the counter, then reached over and grabbed examiner {V} by the collar, pushing {V.him} against the wall behind the counter and shouting that {V.he} was "rigging it." A coworker pulled {DL} away. The lobby camera recorded the incident. {DL} says {D.he} grabbed {VL}'s shirt to keep from falling when {D.he} slipped, and that {D.he} never meant to hurt anyone.
column8: {DL} was at the counter, and the examiners knew {D.him} from earlier tests.

column4: Business Partner Charged With Cutting Brake Lines
column5: With malice, premeditation, and deliberation, attempted to kill {V} by cutting the brake lines of {V.his} truck.
column6: {D} and {V} co-owned a construction company in {HOOD}. They were in a bitter dispute over buying each other out, and a $1 million key-person life insurance policy paid the company if either partner died. On {DATE}, {VL}'s pickup lost its brakes at the bottom of a steep hill and crashed into a ditch; {VL} walked away with bruises. A mechanic found both brake lines cut cleanly about two-thirds through, so they would hold at first and fail under hard braking. The company yard's camera shows {DL} beside {VL}'s truck for six minutes the evening before, after hours. {DL} says {D.he} was checking a tool box {VL} had borrowed, and that the lines must have rusted through.
column8: The yard camera and the insurance motive.

column4: Shopper Charged With 'Returning' Tools Never Bought
column5: Took a 20-volt combo tool kit valued at $389 from the shelves of Tri-County Home Center and, without paying for it, returned it at the service desk without a receipt to obtain a store credit card for $389.
column6: On {DATE} at about 2:47 p.m., {D} took a $389 cordless tool kit from aisle 14 of Tri-County Home Center in {HOOD}, carried it straight to the service desk, and returned it without a receipt for a $389 store credit card, the store says. Loss prevention had flagged {DL}'s driver's license after six earlier no-receipt returns in five weeks, worth $1,751. Store video shows {DL} taking the kit off the shelf. A deputy stopped {DL} in the parking lot at 2:58 p.m. with the credit card in {D.his} wallet, and a warrant search of {D.his} phone found six earlier store cards sold on a resale app for 70 cents on the dollar. {DL} says {D.he} had bought an identical kit at another location and only took a sealed one off the shelf because the box in {D.his} truck was torn.
column8: The store's return system flagged {DL}'s driver's license; loss prevention watched on camera.

column4: County Road Crew Leader Charged in Fuel Card Scheme
column5: Being an employee of Hollis County and entrusted with a county fleet fuel card, fraudulently converted to {D.his} own use $3,960 in fuel purchased with that card for {D.his} personal vehicle.
column6: {D}, a road maintenance crew leader with Hollis County Public Works for eleven years, was assigned fleet fuel card 214 and its personal PIN. A county audit found 38 fill-ups on that card over four months, totaling $3,960, made outside working hours while county truck 214 sat behind the locked gate of the county yard, according to the gate log and the truck's GPS. The last fill-up, at 11:52 p.m. on {DATE}, was recorded by a convenience store camera on {STREET}: {DL} pumping diesel into {D.his} personal red pickup. {DL} says a supervisor, since retired, told {D.him} to fuel {D.his} own truck on emergency callouts, and three of the 38 fill-ups fall on storm nights.
column8: A routine fuel audit matched card 214 to purchases made while truck 214 was locked in the yard.

column4: Stolen Mower and Trailer Found in a Front Yard
column5: Possessed a zero-turn mower and 16-foot utility trailer, together valued at $11,400, belonging to {V}, knowing or having reasonable grounds to believe they had been stolen.
column6: On the night of {DATE}, someone cut the chain on the gate of {V}'s landscaping shop lot in {HOOD} and drove off with a zero-turn mower worth $9,200 on a 16-foot trailer worth $2,200. Nine days later, {V} drove past a single-wide on {STREET} and saw the mower, with its custom orange seat cover and the company decal scraped off, parked in the yard of {D}. The serial number matched. {DL} told deputies {D.he} bought the mower and trailer together for $2,500 cash from a man in a shopping-center parking lot who answered a marketplace listing; the seller's account had been deleted. The State says the price, a trailer with no title, and the scraped decal gave {DL} every reason to know. {DL}'s phone puts {D.him} at home the night of the theft.
column8: {VL} recognized the mower in {DL}'s yard; the serial number matched.

column4: Homeowner Charged After Hail Claim: Insurer Says Damage Was Hammered
column5: With intent to defraud, presented a claim to {D.his} homeowner's insurer for $23,600 to replace {D.his} roof, knowing the claim contained false information about hail damage that {D.he} had caused.
column6: A hailstorm crossed {HOOD} on {DATE}. Three days later, {D} filed a claim for $23,600 to replace the roof of {D.his} house on {STREET}. The insurer's adjuster found 46 round marks on the shingles, nearly all the same size, many cut through the mat, and almost none on the north slope where the storm came from. An engineer hired by the insurer says the marks match a ball-peen hammer. The National Weather Service logged pea- to nickel-sized hail in {HOOD} that night, and two neighbors' minor claims were paid. A neighbor saw {DL} on the roof with a hammer two days after the storm. {DL} says {D.he} was nailing down a lifted ridge cap, and that a twenty-year-old roof bruises easily.
column8: The insurer's adjuster and engineer flagged the damage pattern and referred the claim.

column4: Consignment Shop Owner Charged After Store Closes Owing $11,300
column5: Having been entrusted as consignee with a dining set and a fur coat belonging to {V}, sold them and fraudulently converted to {D.his} own use $2,850 due to {V}.
column6: {D} owned Second Act Consignment in {HOOD} for six years. Consignors were to be paid 60 percent of the sale price within 30 days. When the shop closed on {DATE}, 23 consignors were owed $11,300. {V}, a retired school librarian, had consigned a cherry dining set and a fur coat that sold for $4,750 in the shop's last two months; {VL}'s share, $2,850, was never paid. Bank records show the sale money went into the shop's operating account and out to rent, utilities and a part-time clerk, and that {DL} had drawn no pay for three months, then took a $4,000 check to {D.himself} in the last week. {DL} kept accepting new consignments after the landlord's eviction notice. {DL} says the shop simply ran out of money and that {D.he} has repaid four consignors in part.
column8: Complaints from consignors after the shop closed.

column4: Parent Charged With DWI in Elementary School Pickup Line
column5: Drove a motor vehicle on the car-rider lane of {HOOD} Elementary School, a public vehicular area, while under the influence of an impairing substance and with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, with a child under 18 in the vehicle.
column6: On {DATE} at about 3:05 p.m., {D}'s gray minivan rolled into the back of a stopped SUV in the car-rider line at {HOOD} Elementary School. No one was hurt. {DL}'s seven-year-old was buckled in the back seat. The assistant principal who walked over smelled alcohol and took the keys, and the school resource deputy gave field sobriety tests in the bus loop. An insulated tumbler in the cup holder held white wine. {DL} blew 0.14 on the Intoxilyzer at 4:02 p.m. {DL} says {D.he} had one glass of wine at lunch, that the sun was in {D.his} eyes when the van crept forward, and that {D.his} acid reflux skewed the breath test.
column8: {DL} was behind the wheel when the assistant principal reached the van.

column4: Man Charged After Girlfriend's 911 Call Cut Off Mid-Sentence
column5: Assaulted {V}, a female, by striking {V.him} in the face with his hand, {D} being a male person at least 18 years of age.
column6: On {DATE} at about 11:40 p.m., {V} told {D}, {V.his} boyfriend of two years, that {V.he} was moving out of their apartment on {STREET}. They argued. {V} dialed 911; the call connected for nine seconds. On the recording {V} says "he's—", a man's voice says "give me that," and the line goes dead after a crack. The downstairs neighbor called 911 at 11:44 to report yelling and a thud. Officers arrived at 11:52 and found {V} with a split lip and a swollen left cheek, and {V.his} phone on the floor with a shattered screen. {DL} says {D.he} took the phone so {V} wouldn't "lie to the cops," and that {V} hit {V.his} face on the kitchen counter when they both grabbed for it.
column8: {VL} named {DL}, who was in the apartment when officers arrived.

column4: Bar Stool Swing Leaves Patron With Shattered Cheekbone
column5: Assaulted {V} with a deadly weapon, a wooden bar stool, by striking {V.him} in the face, inflicting serious injury: fractures of the left cheekbone and eye socket requiring surgery.
column6: On {DATE} at about 1:15 a.m., at the Loose Caboose bar on {STREET}, {D} and {V} argued over the pool table. {V}, who had been cut off by the bartender twenty minutes earlier, shoved {DL} backward into the jukebox. The bar's camera, which has no sound, shows four seconds pass; {V} then takes a step toward {DL}, and {DL} picks up a wooden bar stool and swings it into {V}'s face. {V}'s left cheekbone and eye socket were fractured, and a surgeon set them with two titanium plates. {V} is six foot three and about 240 pounds; {DL} is five foot nine and 160. {DL} says {V} had threatened to "put {D.him} through the window" and was coming to do it.
column8: {DL} stayed at the bar and told officers {D.he} swung the stool.

column4: Driver Says Fear of Fake Cop Led to 96 MPH Run From Deputy
column5: Operated a motor vehicle on Route 17 while fleeing and attempting to elude a deputy of the Hollis County Sheriff's Office in the lawful performance of duties, while speeding more than 15 mph over the limit and driving recklessly.
column6: On {DATE} at about 10:50 p.m., a Hollis County deputy in an unmarked gray Charger turned on the grille lights and siren behind {D}'s pickup on Route 17 for 78 mph in a 55. {DL} sped up to 96 mph and ran the red light at Route 17 and {STREET}. At 10:53, {DL} called 911 and said someone with lights was behind {D.him} and {D.he} didn't know if it was a real officer. At 10:54 the dispatcher told {D.him} it was a deputy and to pull over. {DL} slowed to about 60 and drove another 1.6 miles before stopping at a lit gas station at 10:56. The whole run was 4.1 miles. {DL} says {D.he} had read the Sheriff's warning about fake traffic stops and was doing what it said.
column8: {DL} was driving the pickup when it stopped.

column4: Pedestrian Struck, Left on Pruitt Mill Road; Pickup Owner Charged
column5: Being the driver of a vehicle involved in a crash on Pruitt Mill Road that caused serious bodily injury to {V}, and knowing or having reason to know of the crash, willfully failed to stop and remain at the scene.
column6: On {DATE} at about 11:20 p.m., {V} was walking home from a shift at the poultry plant along the shoulder of Pruitt Mill Road when a vehicle struck {V.him} from behind and kept going. A passing driver found {V} in the ditch at 11:35. {V.His} left femur and pelvis were broken. Troopers recovered a piece of a passenger-side mirror housing from a 2014-2018 Chevrolet Silverado, silver. Eleven days later an anonymous caller named {D}, who lives three miles from the scene and drives a silver 2016 Silverado. Its passenger mirror had been replaced with a used one, and its right front fender was dented. {DL} says a deer did the fender two weeks before the crash, a mailbox took the mirror, and {D.he} was home asleep that night.
column8: An anonymous tip, then the salvage yard receipt and the dented fender.

column4: Vape Shop Clerk Charged With Selling Meth Across the Counter
column5: Sold 6.9 grams of methamphetamine, a Schedule II controlled substance, to an undercover detective at Hollis Vapor & Glass on {DATE}.
column6: {D} ran the evening shift at Hollis Vapor & Glass, a vape shop on {STREET} in {HOOD}. After a man arrested with methamphetamine told deputies he bought it from "the night clerk" there, an undercover detective went in twice. Fourteen days before {DATE}, the detective asked {DL} for "an eighth of ice" and paid $150; on {DATE} at 7:15 p.m., a quarter ounce for $280. Both times the shop's own camera shows {DL} unlocking a drawer under the register and weighing the bag on a digital scale. A search warrant served fifteen minutes after the second buy found 14.2 more grams in eight bags in that drawer, opened with a key on {DL}'s key ring, and the $280 in marked bills in {DL}'s front pocket. {DL} says the shop's owner, {OWNER}, kept the drawer stocked and told {D.him} to hand bags to certain customers, and that {D.he} never knew exactly what was in them.
column8: Named by an arrested buyer, then two undercover buys recorded by the shop's own camera.

column4: Landlord's Inspection Turns Up 3D-Printed Pistol
column5: Possessed a firearm, an unserialized 9mm pistol with a 3D-printed frame, after having been convicted of a felony.
column6: {D}, who has a felony drug conviction from about eight years ago, lives with an older brother, {ALT}, in a rented house on {STREET} in {HOOD}. The lease is in {ALT}'s name, with {DL} added as an occupant. On {DATE} at 10:15 a.m., the landlord came for a scheduled inspection; {DL} let the landlord in while {ALT} was at work. In the back bedroom, where {DL} sleeps on a futon, the landlord saw a black pistol on the desk beside a 3D printer. When the landlord asked about it, {DL} said, "It's not loaded, don't worry about it." Deputies returned with a search warrant at 2:05 p.m. and found the pistol, loaded with ten rounds, on the same desk. {DL}'s phone held a photo of the pistol lying on the futon, taken nineteen days earlier. {ALT} says he printed and assembled the pistol himself and that the back room is his workroom as much as anyone's bedroom.
column8: The landlord's call after the inspection.

column4: Ex-Partner Charged After Private Messages Posted From Victim's Own Account
column5: Willfully and without authorization accessed {V}'s email and social media accounts, changing their passwords and recovery information.
column6: {V} ended a two-year relationship with {D} a month before {DATE}. At 11:52 p.m. that night, someone signed into {V}'s email with the password {V} had used for years and that {DL} knew, then used it to reset {V}'s social media password and change the recovery number to a prepaid phone bought with cash the day before. Over the next two nights, {V}'s own account posted screenshots of {V}'s private messages with a friend, captioned as proof that {V} was a liar and a cheat, and messaged {V}'s manager at work. Records obtained by warrant show all three nights' logins came from the internet address assigned to {DL}'s apartment. {DL}'s laptop's browser history had been cleared the morning after the last post. {DL} says the upstairs tenant has used {D.his} Wi-Fi for months and that {D.he} never touched {V}'s accounts.
column8: Warrant returns tracing the logins to the internet account at {DL}'s apartment.

column4: Four Shots Fired Into Home Overnight; No One Hurt
column5: Willfully discharged a firearm into the occupied dwelling of {V} on {STREET}.
column6: At 2:15 a.m. on {DATE}, four shots were fired into {V}'s house on {STREET} in {HOOD}. One went through the front window and into the couch where {V} had been asleep in front of the television until about 1:50 a.m.; {V} was in the bedroom by then, and no one was hurt. Two days earlier, at a cookout, {V} and {D}, a mechanic, had argued over $400 {V} owed {DL} for a car repair, and {DL} said in front of several people, "You'll pay one way or another." A neighbor's doorbell camera recorded a silver sedan passing at 2:15 a.m., consistent with a 2013 to 2018 Nissan Altima; the plate is unreadable. {DL} drives a 2016 silver Altima. A search of {DL}'s home and car found no gun and no ammunition, a gunshot residue test of {DL}'s hands that morning was negative, and {DL}'s phone stayed on the tower near {D.his} apartment, three miles away, all night. {DL} says {D.he} was asleep at home.
column8: {V} named {DL} because of the cookout argument; the doorbell video showed a car like {DL}'s.

column4: Teen Shot Dead Selling Sneakers in Apartment Parking Lot
column5: Killed {V} by shooting {V.him} in the chest during the perpetration of a robbery with a firearm (first-degree murder under the felony murder rule).
column6: {V}, 19, paid for community college by reselling sneakers. A buyer on a resale app agreed to pay $650 for a pair of limited-release shoes, size 11, and set the meeting for 8:40 p.m. on {DATE} in the parking lot of an apartment complex on {STREET} in {HOOD}. {V} drove there with a friend in the passenger seat. The buyer got into the back seat to look at the shoes, pulled a pistol, and said, "Run it." When {V} grabbed for the box, the buyer fired twice, hitting {V} in the chest, and ran with the shoes. {V} died at the hospital at 9:52 p.m. The buyer's account was registered to {D}'s phone number, and the phone's location data put it in the parking lot at the time. Two days later, a search of {DL}'s apartment, four miles away, found the shoe box with {V}'s handwritten inventory label and a 9mm pistol that fired both casings. {DL} says {D.he} lent {D.his} phone that evening to a man {D.he} knew as Dre, who left the shoes and a backpack at {D.his} apartment the next morning.
column7: Friend of {VL}, in the passenger seat
column8: App records tying the buyer account to {DL}'s phone, then the photo lineup.

column4: Shopper Arrested at Harbor Mart Exit Says the TV Was Paid For
