column5: Took and carried away a 65-inch television valued at $1,098, the property of Harbor Mart, without paying for it, on {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE} at about 5:40 p.m., {D} bought a 65-inch television at register 7 at Harbor Mart. The card reader beeped, but the receipt printer jammed and nothing came out. {DL}, due at work at six, pushed the cart toward the exit. A loss prevention associate, {LP}, stepped in front of the cart, took hold of it, and said, "No receipt, no TV. We're not doing this today." {DL} said {D.he} had paid and was late, and started recording on {D.his} phone. {OFFICER} of the Hollis County Sheriff's Office, working an off-duty shift at the store, came over. When {DL} asked whether the law required {D.him} to show a receipt, the officer said, "Yes. It's store policy, and you're on store property." As {DL} kept recording, the officer took the phone out of {D.his} hand and tried to stop the recording, and {DL} pulled {D.his} arm back. {DL} was handcuffed and charged with felony larceny and resisting an officer. The store's register journal shows no completed sale at register 7 at that time. {DL}'s bank app shows a pending $1,184.33 charge from Harbor Mart that afternoon.
column8: Stopped at the exit by loss prevention with the television in the cart.

column4: Two Outboards Vanish From Port Hollis Marina Overnight
column5: Stole two outboard motors valued at $14,600 from boats docked at {FAC} on {DATE}.
column6: At 2:10 a.m. on {DATE}, the camera on the fuel dock at {FAC} recorded a jon boat with its running lights off tie up between slips 14 and 15. Forty minutes later it left, riding low. In the morning, {V} found the twin Yamaha 150s gone from {V.his} center console, and the slip next door had lost one more. Nine days later a Facebook Marketplace listing for a Yamaha 150, "lower unit rebuilt, $3,900 cash," was posted from {D}'s account. A detective answered it, and at {D}'s repair shop on {STREET} in {HOOD} found the advertised motor and a second one with its serial plate ground off. The serial number stamped on the inside of the engine block matched {V}'s. {DL} says {D.he} bought both from a man named Wade at the Cane Creek flea market for parts and didn't know they were stolen.
column8: A Marketplace listing from {D}'s account, then the serial number inside the block.

column4: Harbor Mart Cashier Charged With Loading $11,300 in Unpaid Gift Cards
column5: Embezzled $11,300 belonging to {STORE}, by loading gift cards at register 3 and voiding the cash tenders, between four months before {DATE} and {DATE}.
column6: Over four months, {STORE}'s register 3 recorded 46 gift card loads, each paid in cash and then voided within a minute after the card was activated. The cards, worth $11,300 in all, were drained through online orders shipped to an address on {STREET} in {HOOD}, where {D}'s cousin lives. Every load ran under {D}'s register login. {DL}, a cashier there for two years, says managers used {D.his} login whenever theirs locked, which happened weekly, and that {D.he} never loaded a card {D.he} didn't sell.
column8: An exception report, the register login, and the shipping address.

column4: Fans Turned Away at Stadium Gate Say Local Seller Sold Fake Tickets
column5: Obtained $1,840 from six buyers, including {V}, by selling them counterfeit tickets to a college football game, on or about {DATE}.
column6: In the week before a sold-out rivalry game, {D} posted in a {HOOD} community Facebook group: "4 tickets sec 22 row M, can't go, face value." Six buyers, including {V}, paid a total of $1,840 through a payment app to {D}'s account and received PDF tickets by message. At the stadium gate, all six sets scanned as invalid; several shared the same barcode. {DL} says {D.he} bought the tickets from an online reseller called TixKing, was scammed too, and showed deputies a $300 payment to that account.
column8: The payments went to {DL}'s own account.

column4: Skimmer Found Inside Pump 6; 212 Cards Compromised
column5: Used counterfeit financial transaction cards, encoded with account numbers stolen through a skimmer, to obtain $6,250 in gift cards, on or about {DATE}.
column6: A technician servicing pump 6 at {PLACE.GASSTATION} in {HOOD} found a Bluetooth skimmer wired inside the panel; 212 cards had been swiped there in two weeks. The station's camera showed a person in a gray ball cap opening the pump panel with a key at 4:50 a.m. twelve days earlier. {V}'s card, used at that pump, was then charged for gift cards at three stores. Deputies stopped a gray sedan seen leaving one of those stores; {D} was driving, and 31 blank-white cards encoded with stolen numbers were in the console. {DL} says the car is {D.his} cousin's, the cards were in it when {D.he} borrowed it, and {D.he} has never touched a gas pump panel.
column8: A store lot camera captured the car's plate; {DL} was driving when it was stopped.

column4: Man Posing as Power Company Worker Takes Jewelry From 81-Year-Old
column5: Entered the residence of {V} by deception, falsely claiming to be a power company worker, with intent to commit larceny, on {DATE}.
column6: At about 10:15 a.m. on {DATE}, a man in an orange safety vest knocked at the home of {V}, 81, on {STREET} in {HOOD}, saying he was with the power company and needed to check the wiring in the back bedroom because of a line problem on the street. {V.He} let him in. He was inside twelve minutes. That evening {V} found {V.his} late husband's ring and {V.his} mother's pearls missing from the dresser. A neighbor's doorbell camera recorded the man walking to a white pickup. {V} picked {D} from a photo array five days later, saying, "I think that's him." {DL}, who reads meters part-time for a contractor, says {D.he} was on a route in Cane Creek that morning.
column8: A tip, then a photo array shown by the lead detective.

column4: Rec-League Softball Fight Ends With Player Hospitalized
column5: Assaulted {V} with a deadly weapon, an aluminum softball bat, inflicting serious injury, at {PLACE.PARK} on {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE}, after a close coed rec-league game at {PLACE.PARK}, {V} and {D} argued at the gate between the field and the gravel lot about a play at home plate. Witnesses agree {V} pushed {D} and followed {D.him} toward the cars, shouting. They disagree about what came next. {D} had a bag of bats over {D.his} shoulder. {D.He} pulled one out and swung once. It caught {V} beside the left eye and broke the orbital bone; {V} needed surgery and a titanium plate. {DL} says {V} came at {D.him} with fists raised and {D.he} swung to keep {V} off. Two teammates of {V}'s say {V} had stopped and turned away.
column8: {DL} was at the scene and admitted the swing.

column4: Farmer Charged After Shots Fired Into Truck at Gate
column5: Discharged a firearm into an occupied vehicle, a pickup truck in which {V} was a passenger, while it was in operation, on {DATE}.
column6: Around 11:20 p.m. on {DATE}, three young people who had been driving the back roads near Shiloh pulled a pickup into the gravel entrance of {D}'s farm to turn around. {D}, who had reported two tractor batteries and a welder stolen from the same barn in the past month, came down the hill with a .30-30 rifle and a flashlight. The driver says {D} yelled once and fired as the truck backed out. Two rounds hit the truck: one the tailgate, one the rear window, which spattered glass into the face and neck of {V}, 18, riding in the back seat. {DL} says {D.he} fired twice into the ground as a warning, and the truck came at {D.him} before it reversed.
column8: The driver went straight to the Sheriff's Office; {DL} said at the door that {D.he} had fired.

column4: Tenant Charged With Breaking Into Own Apartment After Lockout
column5: Broke and entered the apartment at Unit 4, {PLACE.APARTMENTS}, with intent to commit larceny therein, on {DATE}.
column6: {D} was two months behind on rent at {PLACE.APARTMENTS}. On {DATE}, while {D} was at work, the landlord, {V}, changed the lock on Unit 4 and taped a notice to the door. No court had ordered an eviction. That night {D} broke the back window, climbed in, and filled two trash bags with clothes, {D.his} child's school things, and a laptop. {V}, who lives across the parking lot, called 911 and told deputies a burglar was carrying property out of the unit. {DL} says everything {D.he} took was {D.his}. {V} says the laptop and a television left in the unit were being held for the back rent under the lease.
column8: Found by the deputy in the parking lot with the bags.

column4: Bar Security Guard Shoots Ejected Patron Outside Door
column5: Assaulted {V} with a deadly weapon, a handgun, with intent to kill, inflicting serious injury, outside {BAR} on {DATE}.
column6: Shortly before closing on {DATE}, {D}, the armed security guard at {BAR}, put {V} out the door after {V} threw a drink at a bartender. Ten minutes later {V} came back up the sidewalk toward the door, shouting, with something dark in {V.his} right hand. {D} drew and fired three times. One round hit {V} in the hip. The object was a phone. {DL} says {V} had told {D.him} on the way out, "I've got something in the car for you," and came back holding the dark object low like a pistol. The bar's door camera shows the approach but not {V}'s hand clearly.

column4: Nurse Robbed at Knifepoint in Hospital Parking Deck
column5: Took a purse and its contents from the person of {V}, by the use of a knife, whereby {V}'s life was threatened, at the parking deck of {PLACE.HOSPITAL} on {DATE}.
column6: At 7:25 a.m. on {DATE}, {V}, a nurse coming off a twelve-hour night shift at {PLACE.HOSPITAL}, was unlocking {V.his} car on level 3 of the parking deck when a man in a gray hoodie held a folding knife to {V.his} side and took {V.his} purse. Forty minutes later {V}'s debit card bought $84 in gas and cigarettes at {PLACE.GASSTATION}. The station camera shows {D}. Two days later {V} picked {D} from a photo array as the man with the knife. {DL} says a man {D.he} knows only as "Junior" gave {D.him} the card to buy gas and {D.he} was nowhere near the hospital.
column8: The station camera, then {V}'s photo array pick.

column4: Postal Inspectors Intercept Fentanyl Pills Bound for Hollis County
column5: Trafficked in an opioid by possessing 4 grams or more but less than 14 grams of fentanyl, in the form of pressed pills, on {DATE}.
column6: A postal inspector in Charlotte flagged a padded envelope bound for Box 214 at the {PLACE.LANDING.TOWN} post office: a handwritten return address that didn't exist, heavy tape, and postage paid in cash. A drug dog alerted, and a federal magistrate signed a warrant. Inside, wrapped in a child's coloring book, were 100 blue pills stamped "M30," which the lab found contained 9.6 grams of fentanyl mixture. Inspectors resealed it and watched the box. On {DATE}, {D} opened Box 214 with a key, took the envelope, and was arrested in the parking lot. The box was rented under the name "Jay Moore" with a fake ID. {DL} says a friend paid {D.him} $50 to pick up "a package" and {D.he} had no idea what was inside.
column8: Arrested after a controlled delivery to the box.

column4: School Crossing Guard Killed; Driver Didn't Stop
column5: Failed to stop at the scene of a crash the defendant knew or reasonably should have known resulted in the death of {V}, near {PLACE.SCHOOL}, on {DATE}.
column6: At 7:48 a.m. on {DATE}, {V}, 68, a crossing guard for twelve years at {PLACE.SCHOOL}, stepped into the marked crosswalk with a stop sign raised. A silver SUV coming out of the sun hit {V} and kept going. {V} died at the hospital that afternoon. Two parents gave partial plates. That evening a trooper found {D}'s SUV in {D.his} garage with a cracked headlight, a dented hood, and {V}'s orange vest fibers in the grille. {DL} says {D.he} was blinded by the sun, felt a hit, thought {D.he} had struck the sign on the curb, and kept driving to a client meeting. {D.He} didn't learn a person had been hit until the trooper came to the door.
column8: Partial plates from two parents, then a door-to-door search of matching SUVs.

column4: Family Paid $18,500 Cash for Mobile Home the Seller Didn't Own
column5: Obtained $18,500 from {V} by falsely representing that {D.he} owned and could sell a mobile home at Lot 9, Pine Haven Mobile Home Park, on or about {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE}, {V} paid {D} $18,500 in cash for a 2004 single-wide at Lot 9 of Pine Haven Mobile Home Park, saved over three years. {D} handed over a bill of sale and said the title would come in the mail. It never did. Two months later a bank repossessed the home: the title was in {D}'s late mother's name, with a lien of $22,000 that hadn't been paid in a year. Records show {D} had sold the same home a year earlier to another buyer, who backed out and got half the money back. {DL} says {D.he} was the heir, believed {D.he} could sell it, and spent the money paying down the lien before the bank "jumped the gun."
column8: {V} reported it after the bank's notice; {DL} signed the bill of sale.

column4: Fire Victims Say They Never Saw Money Raised in Their Name
column5: Obtained $7,400 from donors, including {V}, by falsely representing that the money would go to a family whose home burned, on or about {DATE}.
column6: After a house fire in {HOOD} left a family of five with nothing, {D} set up an online fundraiser with photos of the burned house and organized a pancake breakfast at the fire hall on {DATE}. Donors gave $7,400 in all. {V}, a retired teacher, gave $500. The family received $600 in gift cards and was told the rest "went to costs." Bank records show the online money and the breakfast cash went to {D}'s personal account, then to {D.his} rent, a car repair, and a beach weekend. {DL} says {D.he} was holding the rest for a deposit on a rental house for the family and spent some by mistake from the same account.
column8: The family and donors compared notes and went to the Sheriff's Office.

column4: Dental Assistant Charged With Forging Painkiller Prescriptions
column5: Obtained oxycodone by fraud, by presenting forged prescriptions on the prescription pad of a Hollis County dentist, on {DATE} and on five earlier dates.
column6: A pharmacist at {PHARM} noticed something wrong on {DATE}: a prescription for 30 oxycodone tablets from a dentist, for a patient who'd supposedly had a root canal, written in a dentist's name for a dose dentists almost never write. The pharmacist called the office. The dentist had never seen the patient. The state's prescription database showed six such scripts on the same dentist's pad in two months, at four pharmacies, for four different patient names, all picked up by a person who matched {D}, a receptionist at the practice. Pharmacy cameras at two stores show {D}. {DL} says a former coworker forged them and asked {D.him} to pick them up for "family members who couldn't drive."
column8: Pharmacy cameras at two stores and the pharmacist's recognition.

column4: Foster Parent Charged After Toddler's Arm Broken
column5: Being the caretaker of {V}, a child under 16, intentionally inflicted serious physical injury, a spiral fracture of the left upper arm, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}, three, had lived with {D} as a foster child for five months when {D} brought {V.him} to the emergency room at 8:10 p.m. on {DATE} with a swollen left arm. X-rays showed a spiral fracture of the upper arm. {D} said {V} had fallen from the top bunk while playing with the older foster child, who is seven. The child abuse pediatrician who examined {V} found four bruises on the upper arm in the shape of fingertips, and says a spiral fracture in a three-year-old comes from twisting, not a fall. The defense's expert, a biomechanical engineer, says a child who catches an arm in a bunk bed ladder while falling can twist it the same way. The older foster child told a social worker "{V.he} fell," then later, "I don't know."

column4: Fourteen Scarred Dogs Seized From Shiloh Road Property
column5: Maliciously tortured, mutilated, and cruelly killed animals, by keeping and training dogs for fighting and causing them to fight, on and before {DATE}.
column6: Acting on a tip, deputies and county animal services searched {D}'s property off Shiloh Road on {DATE} with a warrant. They found fourteen pit bull-type dogs, each chained to a buried truck axle out of reach of the others, many with scars on their faces and front legs. In a shed they found a carpet-covered treadmill, a "break stick" used to pry dogs' jaws apart, injectable antibiotics, and a notebook of weights and dates. A shallow grave held two dogs with fresh wounds. {DL} says {D.he} breeds and sells dogs, the scars come from fights when dogs got loose, and a man who rented the back acre used the shed.
column8: The property is {DL}'s, and the notebook's handwriting.

column4: Waterman Says His Crab Pots Were Pulled and Repainted
column5: Stole 32 crab pots and their catch, valued at $2,100, belonging to {V}, from the waters of Bayard Creek, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}, a commercial waterman, set a line of 32 crab pots in Bayard Creek with orange and white buoys carrying {V.his} license number. On {DATE} {V} found the line gone. Two days later a Marine Patrol officer checking licenses at the {PLACE.LANDING} found 30 pots in {D}'s skiff with the buoys freshly painted green and a different license number stenciled on. Under the green paint, the old numbers showed through. {DL} says {D.he} found the pots drifting loose after a storm, abandoned, and had every right to keep them.
column8: A license check at the landing.

column4: Twenty-Year-Old Dies After Motel Party; Friend Charged
column5: Unlawfully sold fentanyl to {V}, and the ingestion of the substance caused the death of {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}, 20, was found unresponsive in Room 112 at {PLACE.MOTEL} at 6:15 a.m., the morning after a birthday party on {DATE} that broke up around 2 a.m. The medical examiner found a fatal level of fentanyl. Texts show {V} asked {D} for "two blues" at 11:48 p.m., and {D} answered "got u." At 12:20 a.m., {V} sent {D} $20 on a payment app with the note "gas." {DL} admits giving {V} two pills from {D.his} own supply, but says {D.he} never sold anything: the $20 was for driving {V} to the party, and {D.he} took the same pills that night. The law requires a sale.
column8: The texts and the payment app on {V}'s phone.

column4: Grandson Charged With Pawning Grandmother's Wedding Ring
column5: Being in a position of trust with {V}, an older adult, knowingly took {V}'s property, a wedding ring and a wristwatch valued at $3,500, by deception, and pawned them, on {DATE}.
column6: {D} moved in with {D.his} grandmother, {V}, 78, a widow, after losing {D.his} apartment. On {DATE}, {D} pawned {V}'s diamond wedding ring and {D.his} late grandfather's gold watch at {PLACE.PAWN} for $650, under {D.his} own name. {V}'s daughter noticed the ring missing from {V}'s hand a week later. {V} first told a deputy {V.he} had never let the ring out of {V.his} sight; at a second interview {V.he} said {V.he} may have told {D} to "take what you need." {V}'s doctor says {V.he} has early memory loss.
column8: The pawn shop's report under {DL}'s own name.

column4: Clerk Robbed at Gunpoint in Sweepstakes Parlor
column5: Took $1,840 in cash from the person and presence of {V}, an employee of Lucky 7 Sweepstakes, by the use and threatened use of a dangerous weapon, a black pistol, whereby {V}'s life was endangered and threatened, on {DATE}.
column6: Just after 1 a.m. on {DATE}, a man in a gray hoodie walked into Lucky 7 Sweepstakes on {STREET} in {HOOD}, pointed a black pistol at the clerk, {V}, and said, "Drawer. Now." {V} handed over $1,840. Deputies stopped {D} eleven minutes later two miles away and found $1,790 in a sock in the console and a black pistol under the seat. The pistol is a Daisy BB pistol made to look like a Glock, with the orange tip painted black. {DL} admits nothing. The defense says a BB pistol, unloaded when found, isn't a dangerous weapon, and the State has to prove {V}'s life was actually endangered.
column8: A traffic stop eleven minutes after the robbery, in a car matching {V}'s description.

column4: Century-Old Tobacco Barn Burns on Family Farm
column5: Willfully and wantonly set fire to and burned a barn, a building used for curing tobacco and storing farm equipment, on {DATE}.
column6: A 1920s log tobacco barn on {D}'s farm outside {HOOD} burned to the ground around 2 a.m. on {DATE}, along with a tractor and a hay baler inside. Six weeks earlier {D} had raised the barn's insurance from $40,000 to $185,000, listing it as "historic." The farm was three payments behind on its equipment loan. The State fire investigator found a pour pattern across the dirt floor and a gas can melted near the doorway, and a lab found gasoline in the soil samples. {DL} says the barn had a wood stove for curing and an old wiring run, that the tractor always leaked fuel, and that {D.he} was asleep at home a mile away when the fire started.
column8: The fire investigator's findings and the insurance records.

column4: Volunteer Fire Department Treasurer Charged in $63,000 Theft
column5: Being the treasurer of the {HOOD} Volunteer Fire Department, a nonprofit corporation, fraudulently embezzled $63,400 entrusted to {D.him} in that capacity, between January and {DATE}.
column6: {D} kept the books for the {HOOD} Volunteer Fire Department for nine years, signing checks and depositing fish fry, raffle, and county money. When the department's new chief tried to buy a $12,000 set of turnout gear in the spring, the bank said the account held $814. An audit found $63,400 missing over fourteen months: cash from fundraisers never deposited and 41 checks written to {DL} marked "reimbursement" with no receipts. Casino records show {DL} spent $58,000 at a casino in Cherokee over the same months. {DL} says the chief and the board approved every reimbursement, that much of the money paid for supplies {D.he} bought with {D.his} own card, and that the department's records were a shoebox mess long before {D.he} took over.
column8: The forensic audit and casino player's card records.

column4: Neighbor's Cattle Sold at Livestock Auction, Farmer Says
column5: Knowingly and designedly, with intent to cheat and defraud, obtained $26,950 from the Hollis Livestock Market by falsely representing that {D.he} owned 22 head of cattle belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} leased pasture next to {D}'s land and ran 40 head of black Angus there. On {DATE}, {D} hauled 22 of them to the Hollis Livestock Market and sold them in the Tuesday sale for $26,950, signing a form swearing the cattle were {D.his}. {V} noticed the herd short a week later. The cattle carried {V}'s ear tags, and the market's video shows {D} unloading them. {DL} says {V} owed {D.him} $31,000 for two years of hay, fencing, and feeding the cattle through a drought, and that {V} told {D.him} to "sell what you need to make it right." {V} says no such conversation ever happened.
column8: The sale barn's consignment form and the ear tags.

column4: Bar Patron's Skull Fractured in Fight With Bouncer
column5: Assaulted {V} with a deadly weapon, a steel tactical flashlight, inflicting serious injury, a skull fracture, on {DATE}.
column6: At closing time on {DATE}, {D}, a bouncer at a bar on {STREET} in {HOOD}, walked {V} out the back door after {V} refused to leave. In the alley, {D} hit {V} once in the head with a 14-inch steel flashlight. {V} fell and fractured {V.his} skull on the curb and spent nine days in the hospital. The alley camera shows {V} turning and raising {V.his} hands toward {D} a second before the swing, but is too grainy to show whether {V} was holding anything. {DL} says {V} had threatened to "cut" {D.him} inside and reached into {V.his} pocket. Deputies found a closed folding knife in {V}'s jacket pocket at the hospital.
column8: The bar's alley camera and {DL}'s own account to officers.

column4: Landscaper's Stolen Trailer and Mowers Found for Sale Online
column5: Possessed a landscaping trailer and two zero-turn mowers valued at $21,500, the property of {V}, knowing and having reasonable grounds to believe them stolen, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s enclosed landscaping trailer, with two zero-turn mowers inside, was taken from the lot behind {V.his} business in {HOOD} over a weekend. Nine days later {V}'s office manager found the mowers listed on Facebook Marketplace at $3,200 each, about a third of their value, by {D}. When a deputy posing as a buyer met {D} at {D.his} shop, the trailer was out back with {V}'s company decals scraped off and the mowers' serial plates ground smooth. {DL} says {D.he} bought everything for $4,000 cash from a man who said he was closing his business, and that {D.he} grinds plates off all the used equipment {D.he} rebuilds.
column8: The Marketplace listing and a deputy posing as a buyer.

column4: Nephew With Power of Attorney Charged in Aunt's Lost Savings
column5: Being in a position of trust and confidence with {V}, an older adult, knowingly by deception used {V}'s funds for {D.his} own benefit, $140,600, between March and {DATE}.
column6: {V}, 88, signed a power of attorney naming {V.his} nephew {D} after a fall two years ago. Over the next nineteen months, $140,600 left {V}'s savings: $62,000 for a pickup truck titled to {D}, $38,000 in transfers to {D}'s account marked "caregiving," and the rest in cash withdrawals. {V}'s nursing home bill went unpaid for five months, and the home moved to discharge {V}. {DL} says {V} wanted {D.him} to have the truck as thanks for taking care of {V.him}, that the caregiving payments were what any aide would charge, and that {D.his} aunt's mind was sharp when {V.he} said so. {V} now has moderate dementia and doesn't remember.
column8: The nursing home's report to Adult Protective Services.

column4: Woman Killed When Golf Cart Overturns on Beach Road
column5: Unlawfully and unintentionally caused the death of {V} while driving a street-legal golf cart while impaired, on {DATE}.
column6: Around 11:30 p.m. on {DATE}, {D} was driving a rented street-legal golf cart on Ocean Drive in Port Hollis after a beach bar's karaoke night, with {V}, a friend from home, in the passenger seat. Taking the turn onto a side street at speed, the cart rolled. {V}, who wasn't wearing the lap belt, was thrown onto the pavement and died of a head injury. {DL}'s blood alcohol concentration was 0.11 two hours later. {DL} says {D.he} had three beers over four hours, that the cart's brakes grabbed and pulled left on the turn, and that the rental company had a complaint about the same cart the week before.
column8: {DL} was at the wheel when officers arrived.

column4: Man Under Protective Order Shows Up at Daughter's Birthday Party
column5: On more than one occasion followed, was in the presence of, and watched {V} without legal purpose while a domestic violence protective order prohibiting that conduct was in effect, causing {V} to fear for {V.his} safety, between October and {DATE}.
column6: {V} has a one-year protective order against {D}, her ex-husband, ordering him to stay 500 feet from her and from their daughter's school except for exchanges set by the custody order. On {DATE} {D} parked across the street from the park pavilion where {V} was holding their daughter's sixth birthday party, sat for an hour, then walked over with a wrapped present and handed it to the girl. A teacher at the party called 911. {V}'s phone log shows {D}'s truck outside her apartment four other nights in three weeks, recorded by her doorbell camera. {DL} says he came to give his daughter a present on her birthday, that the custody order lets him see her, and that he lives two blocks from {V}'s apartment and drives past it to work.
column8: The 911 call from the party, and {V}'s doorbell camera.

column4: Man Took Out Loans in Dead Brother's Name, Prosecutors Say
column5: Knowingly obtained and used the identifying information of {V}, deceased, with intent to fraudulently represent that {D.he} was {V} to obtain credit, a $34,000 car loan and two credit cards, between June and {DATE}.
column6: {V} died of a heart attack three years ago, at 39. In the past eighteen months, someone using {V}'s name, Social Security number, and date of birth took out a $34,000 car loan at a dealership in {CITY} and opened two credit cards that ran up $11,200. The loan defaulted, and the bank's investigator found the death record. The dealership's copy of the driver's license shows {V}'s name with a photo of {D}, {V}'s younger brother, who looks much like {V}. {DL} says {D.his} brother's widow, {ALT}, had all of {V}'s papers and must have done it, using {D.his} photo from a family album, to get back at {D.him} for a fight over the estate.
column8: The license photo in the dealership's loan file.

column4: Woman Caught Walking Out of Grocery With Unpaid Items Again
column5: Stole $86 in groceries and household items from a retail grocery store, on {DATE}.
column6: A loss prevention officer watched {D} slip a $19 scented candle and two packs of batteries into {D.his} purse at a grocery on {DATE}, then pay for a gallon of milk and walk out. {D} has stopped here three times this year for small items, always paying for something cheap. {D} has more than enough in {D.his} account: the receipt in {D.his} purse for the milk was $3. {DL} says {D.he} doesn't know why {D.he} does it, that the urge comes on like a wave, and that {D.he} has been seeing a therapist for it since the spring.
column8: Store camera and a loss prevention officer.

column4: Man Runs From Deputies, Climbs Fence, Gets Stuck
column5: Willfully resisted, delayed, and obstructed a public officer, a sheriff's deputy, in discharging a duty of the officer's office, on {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE} a deputy approached {D} outside a dollar store after a clerk reported a man "casing" the store. When the deputy asked for ID, {D} said, "I didn't do anything," and ran. The deputy chased {D} through a back alley and over a chain-link fence, where {D}'s jacket caught and {D} hung until the deputy arrived. {D} had nothing illegal on {D.him}. {DL} says {D.he} ran because {D.he} had an unpaid ticket and was afraid of being jailed, and that the deputy had no reason to stop {D.him}.
column8: The deputy chased {DL} on foot and caught {D.him} at the fence.

column4: Customer Screams at Cashier, Blocks Parking Lot Lane
column5: Engaged in disorderly conduct in a public place by making a public disturbance in a retail store parking lot, on {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE}, {D} tried to return a $240 space heater to a home goods store without a receipt and was refused. {D} began shouting at the cashier, followed {D.him} into the parking lot, stood in the lane blocking cars, and screamed that the store was "robbing people." A manager called deputies after {D} refused to move for ten minutes. {DL} says {D.he} was upset because the heater had been a gift for {D.his} mother and that the manager was rude.
column8: The manager's call and the lot camera.

column4: Fisherman Charged With Trespass at Private Pond
column5: Entered and remained on premises of {V}, a private farm pond, after being notified not to enter, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} owns a farm outside {HOOD} with a stocked pond. After finding trash and a cut fence, {V} posted four "No Trespassing" signs and told {D} personally, a month earlier, not to fish there. On {DATE}, {V} saw {D}'s truck at the gate and found {D} fishing at the pond with two coolers. {D} says the signs were hidden by brush, that {V}'s earlier warning was about the creek, and that the pond has been fished by locals for fifty years.

column4: Man Stopped for Taillight Was Driving on Revoked License
column5: Drove a motor vehicle on a public highway while {D.his} driver's license was revoked, on {DATE}.
column6: A trooper stopped {D} on {DATE} at 5:40 a.m. for a broken taillight. A records check showed {D}'s license had been revoked eight months earlier after {D} failed to pay a fine and missed a court date on a speeding ticket. {D} was on the way to a 6 a.m. shift at a poultry plant twenty-two miles away, with no bus line and no one to carry {D.him}. {DL} says {D.he} didn't know the revocation was still in effect because the notice went to an old address.

column4: Deputies Find Marijuana in Glove Box During Traffic Stop
column5: Knowingly possessed marijuana, a Schedule VI controlled substance, in an amount of half an ounce or less, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy stopped {D} on {DATE} for a rolling stop at a four-way. The deputy smelled marijuana, searched the car, and found a sandwich bag with 6 grams in the glove box and a grinder in the console. {DL} says the car is a shared family car, that {D.his} cousin used it all week and left the bag, and that {D.he} never opened the glove box. The defense moves to suppress: the deputy had the smell of marijuana but hemp products also smell the same, and the State has no lab report separating legal hemp from marijuana.
column8: A traffic stop and a vehicle search.

column4: Argument Over Parking Space Ends With a Shove
column5: Assaulted {V} by pushing {V.him} in the chest with both hands, on {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE}, after a funeral at a church in {HOOD}, {D} and {V} reached the last parking space near the door at the same time. Words were exchanged. {D} got out and walked to {V}'s window. According to {V}, {D} shoved {V.him} in the chest when {V.he} got out of the car, and {V.he} stumbled into the neighboring bumper. {D} says {V} stepped toward {D.him} with a closed fist and {D.he} put out {D.his} hands to keep {V.him} back. A church usher saw part of it.
column8: Both men stayed at the scene.

column4: Unlocked Trucks Hit Overnight in Contractor Subdivision
column5: Broke into and entered a motor vehicle belonging to {V}, with intent to commit larceny therein, on {DATE}.
column6: Overnight on {DATE}, five trucks parked in a subdivision were entered and ransacked. {V}'s truck lost a $400 cordless drill set and a nail gun. A doorbell camera two houses down recorded a man in a gray hoodie with a flashlight moving from truck to truck at 2:10 a.m. A deputy saw {D} walking nearby twenty minutes later with a duffel bag containing a drill set, a nail gun, and a flashlight. {DL} says {D.he} found the bag on the roadside and was walking home.
column8: A deputy stopped {DL} with the stolen tools.

column4: Student Charged After Pills Found in Backpack at Traffic Stop
column5: Knowingly possessed amphetamine, a Schedule II controlled substance, on {DATE}.
column6: A trooper stopped {D} on {DATE} for speeding and searched the car after {D} consented. In the backpack was an unlabeled sandwich bag with 22 pills identified as amphetamine salts (Adderall). {D} has no prescription. {DL} says a friend gave {D.him} the pills to hold during exams, that {D.he} never took any, and that {D.he} forgot they were in the backpack.
column8: A traffic stop and a consent search.

column4: Stolen Bicycles Turn Up in Pawn Shop; Seller Charged
column5: Stole a bicycle valued at $480 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s $480 commuter bicycle was cut from a bike rack outside the {HOOD} public library on {DATE}. Four days later, {D} sold a bicycle matching its description to a pawn shop, handing over a state ID and signing the pawn ticket. {V}'s serial number matches. {DL} says {D.he} bought the bike for $60 from a man outside the library and didn't know it was stolen.
column8: The pawn ticket and the serial number.

column4: Driver Filled Tank and Drove Off Without Paying
column5: Stole $64 in motor fuel from a gas station, on {DATE}.
column6: A gas station camera recorded {D} filling a tank with $64 of fuel at pump six at 11:20 p.m. on {DATE}, then driving away without going inside. The plate was readable and came back to {D}. {DL} says the card reader at the pump was broken, that {D.he} meant to pay inside, and that {D.he} was rushing to a sick relative's house.
column8: The pump camera and the plate.

column4: Bar Window Smashed After Closing; Customer Charged
column5: Willfully and wantonly injured personal property of {V}, a plate glass window, causing damage of $1,400, on {DATE}.
column6: After being cut off and asked to leave a bar at 1:50 a.m. on {DATE}, {D} walked outside, threw a beer bottle through the front plate glass window, and stood on the sidewalk until deputies arrived. {V}, the bar owner, put the replacement cost at $1,400. {DL} says {D.he} threw the bottle at a trash can and the window was already cracked.
column8: The bar's front camera and the owner's call.

column4: Man Banned From Library Returns, Charged With Trespass
column5: Entered and remained on the premises of the county public library after being notified not to enter, on {DATE}.
column6: The county library gave {D} a written notice not to return for six months after {D} was caught sleeping in the stacks and arguing with a librarian. On {DATE}, a librarian saw {D} reading at a table, called deputies, and {D} was arrested. {DL} says {D.he} never received the notice, since it was mailed to a shelter {D.he} had left, and that the library is a public building.

column4: Neighbor's Riding Mower Missing From Shed, Found Next Door
column5: Stole a riding lawn mower valued at $900 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s riding mower disappeared from an unlocked shed on {DATE}, after {V} refused to lend it to {D}, a neighbor, because {D} had broken a blade the year before. A week later, {V} saw the mower in {D}'s backyard with the blade deck freshly cleaned. {DL} says {V} had told {D.him} to "use it whenever," and that {D.he} was going to return it after cutting {D.his} yard.

column4: Dog Walk Argument Ends in Shove and a Charge
column5: Assaulted {V} by pushing {V.him} to the ground, on {DATE}.
column6: {D}'s unleashed dog ran at {V}'s small dog in a county park on {DATE}. {V} yelled, and {D} yelled back. According to {V}, {D} shoved {V.him} to the ground and {V} scraped {V.his} hands. {D} says {V} swung a leash at {D.his} dog and {D.he} pushed {V.him} away to protect it.
column8: Both stayed and deputies were called.

column4: Man Reported Car Stolen, Deputies Find It at Girlfriend's House
column5: Willfully made a false report to law enforcement that {D.his} car had been stolen, on {DATE}.
column6: {D} called the sheriff's office on {DATE} to report a car stolen from outside {D.his} apartment. A deputy found the car two days later at {D}'s girlfriend's house, parked behind a shed. {D} said the girlfriend had no right to take it. The girlfriend said {D} had loaned it to her and filed the report after they broke up. {DL} says {D.he} truly believed the car was taken without permission.
column8: A deputy followed up on the report.

column4: Doorbell Camera Catches Porch Package Thief
column5: Stole a package containing a pair of boots valued at $140 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: On {DATE}, {V}'s doorbell camera recorded a man in a delivery-style vest picking up a package from the porch and walking off. Two other neighbors reported missing parcels the same week. {V} identified {D} from the video at the grocery store. {DL} says {D.he} was a delivery driver for an app and picked up the wrong porch by mistake.
column8: {V}'s doorbell camera and a chance sighting.

column4: Teens Take Golf Cart for a Midnight Ride Through Subdivision
column5: Took and carried away a golf cart valued at $2,900 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s golf cart was taken from a carport near midnight on {DATE}, driven around a subdivision with its lights off, and abandoned in a retention pond. A neighbor's camera showed {D} and a friend riding on the cart. {DL} says the friend took it and {D.he} only hopped on for a ride.

column4: Man Refuses to Give Name to Deputy, Charged With Resisting
column5: Willfully resisted, delayed, and obstructed a public officer, a sheriff's deputy, by refusing to identify {D.himself} during a lawful stop, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy approached {D} sitting in a parked car at a closed county park at 11 p.m. on {DATE}. {D} refused to give a name or show ID, saying, "I know my rights." The deputy ordered {D} out of the car; {D} refused, rolled up the window, and was arrested. {DL} says the park had no sign about closing hours and that the deputy had no reason to stop {D.him}.

column4: Woman Carried Mother's Pain Pills in Her Purse, Deputies Say
column5: Knowingly possessed oxycodone, a Schedule II controlled substance, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy stopped {D} for a broken tail light on {DATE}. A pill bottle in {D}'s purse had another person's name on the label: {D}'s mother, with 38 oxycodone tablets. {DL} says {D.he} was picking up the prescription for {D.his} mother, who is bedridden, and was on the way to deliver it.

column4: Customers Skip Out on $74 Diner Bill
column5: Stole $74 in food and service from a diner, on {DATE}.
column6: {D} and a friend ate a $74 meal at a diner on {DATE}, and while the waitress was in the kitchen, walked out the front door and drove away. The diner's camera caught the plate. {DL} says the waitress had told them to pay at the counter and they had been looking for the register.

column4: Neighbor Dispute Over Property Line Ends With Broken Fence
column5: Willfully and wantonly damaged real property of {V}, a wooden privacy fence, causing damage of $850, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} built a privacy fence on {V.his} side of what {D} believes is {D}'s property line. On {DATE}, {D} kicked in six boards and pulled two posts loose with a truck chain. {V}'s doorbell camera recorded the whole thing. A survey later put the fence two feet over {V}'s own line. {DL} says {D.he} warned {V} first and had every right.

column4: Man Used Found Credit Card at Gas Pumps, Prosecutors Say
column5: Used a credit card belonging to {V}, a card issued in another person's name, to obtain $212 in goods and services, without consent, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} lost a wallet at a grocery store on {DATE}. Within two hours, the credit card inside was used four times: twice at a gas station and twice at a convenience store, for $212 total. The gas station camera showed {D} swiping the card. {DL} says {D.he} found the wallet in a parking lot, meant to turn it in, and used the card only to buy gas to drive to the sheriff's office.
column8: The gas station camera and the card number.

column4: Shopper Swapped Price Stickers at Hardware Store
column5: Stole $126 in tools from a hardware store by switching price labels, on {DATE}.
column6: A hardware store manager watched {D} peel a $14 sticker from a box of washers and stick it over the label on a $140 drill bit set on {DATE}. {D} paid $14 at the register and left. {DL} says the stickers had fallen off the shelf display and {D.he} grabbed what was on the floor.

column4: Moped Rider Leads Deputy on Chase Through Backyards
column5: Operated a motor vehicle on a street while fleeing from a law enforcement officer who was attempting to stop the vehicle, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy turned on blue lights behind {D}'s moped for a missing tail light on {DATE}. {D} sped up to about 30 mph, cut through three backyards, and knocked over a clothesline before the moped ran out of gas. {DL} says {D.he} didn't see the lights and had earbuds in.

column4: Late-Night Party Ends With Disorderly Conduct Charge
column5: Engaged in disorderly conduct by making a public disturbance, loud music and shouting after repeated warnings, on {DATE}.
column6: Deputies were called to {D}'s house at 11:10 p.m. and again at 1:20 a.m. on {DATE} for loud music. At the second visit {D} came onto the lawn yelling that the neighbors were "snitches" and refused to turn the speaker down. Two neighbors with infants signed complaints. {DL} says the party was a birthday and {D.he} was never told about the first visit.

column4: Teen Popped Wheelies on County Road Near School
column5: Drove a motor vehicle on a highway carelessly and heedlessly in willful disregard of the rights and safety of others, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy saw {D} popping wheelies on a dirt bike at about 45 mph down a county road beside an elementary school at dismissal on {DATE}, weaving between cars. {D} has no license. {DL} says {D.he} was on a road with no traffic and didn't see any children.

column4: Graffiti Covers Highway Underpass Wall
column5: Willfully and wantonly damaged real property of {V}, a concrete underpass wall, causing damage of $1,800, on {DATE}.
column6: A 40-foot wall of a highway underpass was covered overnight on {DATE} with a spray-painted tag. The state transportation department put cleanup at $1,800. A deputy found {D} in a parked car near the underpass at 4 a.m. with eleven cans of paint and paint on {D.his} hands. {DL} says {D.he} was only bringing cans for a friend who painted a legal mural.
column8: A deputy's patrol and a highway camera.

column4: Prank 911 Call Sent Fire Trucks to Ex's House
column5: Willfully made a false report to law enforcement that a house was on fire, on {DATE}.
column6: A man called 911 at 9:50 p.m. on {DATE} to report flames visible at a house on a quiet road. Two engines and a deputy arrived to find no fire, only the residents, {D}'s ex-wife and her new partner, eating dinner. The call came from a prepaid phone that was later traced to a store where {D} paid cash. {DL} says {D.he} was nowhere near and that anyone could have used {D.his} number.
column8: Phone records traced to a store.

column4: Man Flashed Toy Badge at Convenience Store
column5: Falsely pretended to be a law enforcement officer, displaying a badge, to obtain a benefit, on {DATE}.
column6: A clerk says {D} flashed a gold badge at a convenience store counter on {DATE}, said, "Sheriff's office, I get the discount," and was handed a $7 sandwich for free. The badge turned out to be a costume piece from a novelty store. {DL} says it was a joke and the clerk laughed.
column8: The clerk's report and the store camera.

column4: Woman Carried Pistol in Purse at County Fair
column5: Carried a concealed handgun, a .380 pistol, on and about {D.his} person without a permit, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy saw the grip of a pistol in the open top of {D}'s purse at the county fair on {DATE} when {D} set it on a table. {D} had no concealed carry permit. {DL} says the purse was a gift from {D.his} late husband, that the pistol was a keepsake {D.he} carried to the fair to show a friend, and that {D.he} didn't know it needed a permit.
column8: A deputy's sight of the grip.

column4: Dog Left Chained Without Water in August Heat
column5: Intentionally deprived an animal, a dog, of necessary sustenance, water, in the owner's care, on {DATE}.
column6: Animal control found {D}'s hound chained to a post in the yard on {DATE} in 97-degree heat with an empty water bowl and no shade. The dog was lethargic and panting. {D} was at work. {DL} says the dog had a full bowl that morning and a neighbor must have kicked it over.
column8: A neighbor's call to animal control.

column4: Driver Backed Into Parked Car and Left
column5: As the driver of a vehicle involved in a crash with an attended vehicle, failed to stop and give identifying information, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} sat in a parked car at a drugstore on {DATE} when a pickup backed into it, crushing the rear bumper and fender, and left. {V} wrote down the plate. The truck belongs to {D}. {DL} says {D.he} felt a bump but thought it was a cart and didn't see anyone in the other car.
column8: {V}'s plate note and the drugstore camera.

column4: Farmer Wrote $380 Check on Closed Account
column5: Uttered a check for $380 drawn on an account {D} knew was closed, to a feed store, on {DATE}.
column6: {D} wrote a $380 check to a feed store for hay and sweet feed on {DATE}. The check came back marked 'account closed.' The bank had closed the account four months earlier after repeated overdrafts and mailed notice. The store left three messages. {DL} says the bank never told {D.him} and {D.he} was waiting on a government payment.

column4: Man Posted Threat to Burn Neighbor's Truck
column5: Willfully threatened to damage the property of {V} by fire, in a manner a reasonable person would believe would be carried out, on {DATE}.
column6: After {V} complained about {D}'s barking dogs, {D} posted on a neighborhood Facebook group on {DATE}: "Tell {V} I'll light that truck up if the complaints don't stop." A dozen neighbors saw it. {V} showed it to deputies the next morning. {DL} says it was a joke made in front of friends and he deleted it within an hour.

column4: Man Sent 200 Texts to Ex After Being Blocked
column5: Willfully on more than one occasion harassed {V} without legal purpose, including 212 text messages and calls after being told to stop, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} ended a relationship with {D} in the spring and told {D} to stop contacting {V.him}. Over the next six weeks {D} sent 212 text messages from three different numbers, left voicemails, and appeared once outside {V}'s workplace. {V} blocked each number and kept screenshots. {DL} says {D.he} never threatened {V.him} and only wanted closure.

column4: Man Found Asleep on Neighbor's Porch Swing at 4 A.M.
column5: Entered and remained on the premises of {V} after being notified not to enter, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} woke at 4 a.m. on {DATE} to a noise on the front porch and found {D} asleep on the porch swing with a coat over {D.his} head. {D} smelled of beer. {V} had told {D} the week before to stay off {V.his} property after an argument over a fence. {DL} says {D.he} thought it was {D.his} own porch, since the houses look alike.

column4: Mail From Six Boxes Found in Man's Car
column5: Stole mail belonging to several residents of a rural route, valued at less than $1,000, on {DATE}.
column6: Six residents on a rural route reported missing mail over two weeks, including a birthday card with $50 and a pharmacy package. A deputy stopped {D} for a headlight on {DATE} and found nineteen pieces of opened mail addressed to other people in a grocery bag in {D}'s back seat. {DL} says {D.he} found the bag at a mailbox cluster and was bringing it to the post office.

column4: Man Caught Siphoning Gas From Neighbor's Truck
column5: Stole about twenty gallons of gasoline valued at $74 from a pickup truck belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} came out at 5:40 a.m. on {DATE} and found {D} crouched at {V}'s truck with a hose in the tank and a five-gallon can. {D} said {D.he} had run out of gas and was borrowing a little. {V} found the tank nearly empty and two more filled cans in {D}'s car. {DL} says {V} had lent {D.him} gas before.

column4: All Four Tires Slashed After Breakup
column5: Willfully and wantonly injured personal property of {V}, a car, by slashing four tires, causing damage of $640, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} came out on {DATE} to find all four tires on {V.his} car slashed. A neighbor's camera showed a man in a gray jacket walk along the car at 2:10 a.m. {V} had ended a relationship with {D} the week before. {DL} says {D.he} was asleep and that gray jackets are common.

column4: Football Tailgate Argument Ends in a Shove
column5: Assaulted {V} by shoving {V.him} with both hands, on {DATE}.
column6: At a high school football tailgate on {DATE}, {D} and {V} argued about a folding table that blocked a parking space. According to {V}, {D} shoved {V.him} hard enough to knock {V.him} into a cooler. {D} says {V} had been drinking and stepped into {D.his} chest. A parent filmed the end.

column4: Driver Gave His Brother's Name at Traffic Stop
column5: Willfully and unlawfully delayed and obstructed a public officer by giving a false name during a lawful stop, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy stopped {D} for speeding on {DATE}. {D} had no license on {D.him} and gave the name of {D.his} brother, with the brother's date of birth. The deputy wrote a citation in that name. The brother's license was clean, and a fingerprint check at the jail revealed {D}'s true identity. {DL} says {D.he} panicked because of an unpaid fine.

column4: Aluminum Gutters Stripped From Vacant House
column5: Stole aluminum gutters and downspouts valued at $620 belonging to {V}, from a vacant house, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} owns a vacant rental house that was being renovated. Over a weekend on {DATE}, someone stripped all the aluminum gutters and downspouts. A scrap yard record shows {D} sold 70 pounds of aluminum gutters for $42 the next Monday. {DL} says {D.he} bought a load from a man at a flea market.

column4: Laptop Taken From Library Table Found at Pawn Shop
column5: Possessed a laptop computer valued at $780 belonging to {V}, knowing and having reasonable grounds to believe it stolen, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}, a student, stepped away from a library table on {DATE} for five minutes and returned to find {V.his} laptop gone. Two days later the laptop was pawned by {D} at a pawn shop. {V}'s serial number matched. {DL} says {D.he} bought the laptop for $100 from a man in the parking lot.

column4: Woman Returned Stolen Goods for Store Credit
column5: Obtained $284 in store credit from a retail store by falsely representing that merchandise had been purchased, on {DATE}.
column6: A department store's return desk gave {D} $284 in store credit on {DATE} for a coat and two sweaters with a receipt. A loss prevention officer noticed the receipt numbers matched a receipt from an earlier purchase of different items. The coat and sweaters still had security tags from the sales floor. {DL} says a friend gave {D.him} the merchandise and receipt as a gift.
column8: The loss prevention officer's receipt check.

column4: Underage Man Used Fake License to Buy Beer
column5: Possessed a forged driver's license with intent to utter it, on {DATE}.
column6: A gas station clerk scanned {D}'s driver's license on {DATE} while selling a twelve-pack, and the scanner flagged it. The license listed {D} as 24 and carried another man's name. {D} is 19. A deputy found a second fake license in {D}'s wallet. {DL} says {D.he} bought the licenses online as novelty items.

column4: Man Walked Out With $400 in Paint
column5: Stole $412 in paint from a retail merchant, concealing it in a bag, on {DATE}.
column6: A home improvement store camera recorded {D} placing five gallons of paint, each $82, into a large backpack in the paint aisle on {DATE} and walking out past the registers. {D} was stopped in the lot. {DL} says {D.he} was painting for a landlord who had promised to pay and that {D.he} meant to pay.
column8: The store camera and the manager.

column4: Dumpster Fire Behind Restaurant Called Arson Attempt
column5: Willfully and wantonly injured personal property of {V}, a commercial dumpster, by fire, causing damage of $900, on {DATE}.
column6: A dumpster behind a restaurant burned on {DATE} at 2 a.m. The fire was out before it reached the building. {V}, the owner, had fired {D} the day before for no-call, no-show. The kitchen's back camera showed a person in a hooded jacket lighting something near the dumpster. {DL} says {D.he} was at a friend's house.

column4: Man Took Tip Jar From Coffee Shop Counter
column5: Stole $86 in cash from a tip jar belonging to {V}, a coffee shop, on {DATE}.
column6: A man walked into a coffee shop on {DATE} while the barista was in the back, lifted the tip jar from the counter, and ran out. The jar held $86. {V}, the owner, saw it on the camera. {D} was stopped by a deputy a block away holding a handful of bills. {DL} says {D.he} found the jar on the sidewalk.
column8: The shop camera and a deputy's quick stop.

column4: Backyard Shed Broken Into, Tools Gone
column5: Broke and entered a building, a backyard storage shed belonging to {V}, with intent to commit larceny therein, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s backyard shed was pried open on {DATE} and a leaf blower, a mower blade, and a set of wrenches taken. A deputy later found a mower blade matching {V}'s in {D}'s garage. {D} lives two houses away. {DL} says {D.he} bought the blade at a yard sale.

column4: Digital Scale and Baggies Found in Car at Traffic Stop
column5: Knowingly possessed drug paraphernalia, a digital scale and plastic bags, with intent to package a controlled substance, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy stopped {D} for running a stop sign on {DATE} and found a digital scale and a roll of small plastic bags in the console. A drug dog alerted but no drugs were found. {DL} says {D.he} sells handmade jewelry at craft fairs and uses the scale for beads.
column8: A traffic stop and a dog sniff.

column4: Teens Say Man Pointed Pistol at Them From Car
column5: Assaulted {V} by pointing a gun, an airsoft pistol that appeared to be a handgun, on {DATE}.
column6: Three teenagers walking home on {DATE} told deputies a driver pulled alongside them and pointed a black pistol out the window, yelling, "Get off my road." {V} said it looked real and ran into a yard. Deputies stopped {D} a mile away and found an airsoft pistol on the seat. {DL} says it was a toy and the boys had thrown a bottle at the car.
column8: The teens' description and a deputy's stop.

column4: Man Caught Prying Open Vending Machine Behind Car Wash
column5: Willfully and wantonly injured personal property of {V}, a vending machine, causing damage of $640, on {DATE}.
column6: A vending company owner found the coin box of a drink machine behind a car wash pried open on {DATE}. A camera showed a man with a crowbar. {D} was stopped nearby with $38 in quarters and a crowbar in the truck. {DL} says {D.he} found the quarters in a parking lot.
column8: The car wash camera and a deputy's stop.

column4: Parent Screams at School Bus Driver in Front of Children
column5: Engaged in disorderly conduct by making a public disturbance at a school bus stop, on {DATE}.
column6: {D} stood in front of a school bus on {DATE}, blocking it, and yelled at the driver for ten minutes about a seating dispute with {D.his} son. Twenty children watched. The driver radioed dispatch and a deputy came. {DL} says the driver had been rough with the boy.
column8: The bus camera and the driver's radio call.

column4: Four Tires and Rims Missing From Customer's Car at Junkyard
column5: Possessed four tires and rims valued at $780 belonging to {V}, knowing and having reasonable grounds to believe them stolen, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} woke on {DATE} to find {V.his} truck on cinder blocks, the wheels gone. A week later, a deputy found four matching tires and rims in {D}'s yard with the lug nut pattern scratched. {DL} says {D.he} bought them for $200 at a flea market.
column8: A deputy's tip and a search with consent.

column4: Hunter's Stand Found on Posted Land
column5: Entered and remained on the premises of {V}, a posted hunting tract, after being notified not to enter, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s 40-acre tract was posted with orange paint on the trees. On {DATE}, {V}'s trail camera caught {D} climbing into a deer stand at 5:30 a.m. {D}'s truck was parked on a county road at the edge. {DL} says the paint was faded and {D.he} thought the tract was the neighbor's, who had given permission.

column4: Flag and Pole Taken From Veteran's Front Yard
column5: Stole a flag and flagpole valued at $240 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}, a retired Marine, found {V.his} flagpole and 3-by-5 flag missing from the front yard on {DATE}. A neighbor's camera showed a truck backing up at 1:15 a.m. The flag turned up draped in {D}'s truck bed. {DL} says {D.he} took it as a prank and meant to return it.
column8: A neighbor's camera and a deputy's tip.

column4: Man Kept Friend's Truck for Three Weeks
column5: Stole a pickup truck valued at $900 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} lent {D} an old pickup for a weekend job on {DATE}. {D} kept it for three weeks, ignored {V}'s calls, and was seen driving it across the county. {V} reported it stolen. {DL} says {V} owed {D.him} $400 for work and said to keep it until paid.

column4: Church Donation Box Emptied
column5: Stole $212 in cash from a donation box belonging to {V}, a church, on {DATE}.
column6: A church secretary found the donation box in the vestibule empty on {DATE}. A camera showed {D} leaving at 2:10 p.m. with a folded coat over an arm and a bulge. {DL} says {D.he} stopped to pray and the coat held {D.his} own papers.

column4: Teen on Skateboard Ignored Deputy's Order to Stop
column5: Willfully resisted, delayed, and obstructed a public officer, a sheriff's deputy, in discharging a duty of the officer's office, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy told {D} to stop skateboarding on a church's steps on {DATE}. {D} kicked off, rolled away, and refused to give a name when the deputy caught up. The deputy took {D}'s arm and {D} pulled loose. {DL} says the steps were public and the deputy never explained why.

column4: Tenant Pulled Apartment Fire Alarm After Argument
column5: Willfully made a false report that a building was on fire by pulling a fire alarm, on {DATE}.
column6: Three engines were dispatched to an apartment building at 2:05 a.m. on {DATE} when the alarm sounded. There was no fire. A hallway camera showed {D} pulling the lever after arguing with a neighbor. {DL} says {D.he} tripped and caught the lever.

column4: Woman Took Clothes From Laundromat Dryer
column5: Stole clothing valued at $210 belonging to {V}, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} left a load of laundry in a laundromat dryer on {DATE} and came back to find the dryer empty. The camera showed {D} taking the clothes into a black bag and leaving. {DL} says {D.he} thought the dryer was {D.his} and had left a similar load there.

column4: Rec League Softball Dispute Ends in a Punch
column5: Assaulted {V}, an umpire, by striking {V.him} in the face with a fist, on {DATE}.
column6: During a rec league softball game on {DATE}, {D}, a coach, argued a called third strike with {V}, the umpire. According to {V}, {D} hit {V.him} in the face when {V.he} turned to leave. {D} says {V} stepped on {D.his} foot and {D.he} pushed {V.him} off.

column4: Facebook Seller Sold Fake Concert Tickets
column5: Obtained $240 from {V} by falsely representing that {D} was selling genuine concert tickets, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} paid {D} $240 on {DATE} for two concert tickets listed on a Facebook marketplace page. At the venue, the barcodes were rejected as duplicates. A second buyer had the same tickets. {DL} says {D.he} bought the tickets legitimately and never knew they were copies.
column8: The venue's duplicate scan and {V}'s complaint.

column4: Neighbor's Doorbell Camera Smashed, Man Charged
column5: Willfully and wantonly injured personal property of {V}, a doorbell camera, causing damage of $230, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}'s doorbell camera, installed after a package theft, was smashed with a hammer on {DATE}. The camera uploaded the last seconds to its cloud: {D}, {V}'s neighbor, swinging the hammer. {DL} says the camera pointed into {D.his} bedroom window.

column4: Passenger Ran From Rideshare Without Paying $38 Fare
column5: Stole $38 in transportation services from {V}, a rideshare driver, on {DATE}.
column6: {V}, a rideshare driver, took {D} 14 miles on {DATE} at 12:40 a.m. At the drop-off, {D} said {D.he} was getting cash and ran into a house. The fare was $38. {V}'s dash camera recorded the exchange. {DL} says {D.he} had a card that was declined and meant to return with cash.
column8: {V}'s dash camera and the ride record.

column4: Man Cut Off Wheel Boot With Bolt Cutters
column5: Willfully and wantonly injured personal property of {V}, a wheel immobilizer, causing damage of $450, on {DATE}.
column6: A towing company put a boot on {D}'s car for parking in a private lot without a permit on {DATE}. {D} cut the boot off with bolt cutters and drove away. The boot, worth $450, was ruined. {DL} says the lot had no signs and the boot was unlawful.

column4: Daytime Break-In Empties Jewelry Box While Family Was at Work
column5: Broke and entered a dwelling house of {V} with intent to commit larceny therein, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} came home from work on {DATE} to find the back door kicked in and a jewelry box and a laptop gone. A neighbor's doorbell camera showed a man in a green hooded sweatshirt at the back gate at 11:20 a.m. A pawn shop took in a ring matching {V}'s description that afternoon from {D}. {DL} says {D.he} bought the ring from a friend and was never at the house.
column8: The pawn shop's ticket and a neighbor's camera.

column4: Man Slides Demand Note to Teller, Leaves With $2,100
column5: Took $2,100 in United States currency from the person and presence of {V}, a bank teller, by putting {V.him} in fear, on {DATE}.
column6: A man in a ball cap handed {V}, a bank teller, a note on {DATE} that said 'Put the money in the bag, no dye pack, no alarm.' {V} handed over $2,100 and triggered a silent alarm. The man walked out. Deputies stopped {D} three blocks away with a cap and $1,640 in bills. {DL} says {D.he} had cashed a paycheck at another bank and has never been inside this branch.
column8: The bank's alarm and a deputy's stop.

column4: Deputies Find Packaged Cocaine in Driver's Console
column5: Possessed with intent to sell or deliver cocaine, a Schedule II controlled substance, on {DATE}.
column6: A deputy stopped {D} for a headlight on {DATE} and smelled marijuana. In the console were fourteen small bags of white powder, a digital scale, and $720 in small bills. The lab found cocaine in all fourteen, about 9 grams total. {DL} says the bags belonged to a passenger who got out minutes earlier and that the cash was {D.his} rent money.

column4: Warehouse Worker Sold Oxycodone to Coworkers
column5: Delivered oxycodone, a Schedule II controlled substance, to another person, on {DATE}.
column6: A warehouse worker told a supervisor that {D} sold oxycodone in the break room. Deputies set up a controlled buy on {DATE}: the worker, wearing a wire, bought six pills for $90 from {D}. {DL} says the worker asked for a favor and {D.he} gave pills from {D.his} own prescription without charging.
column8: A coworker's report and a controlled buy.

column4: Woman Says Boyfriend Choked Her During Argument
column5: Assaulted {V} and inflicted physical injury by strangulation, on {DATE}.
column6: {V} called 911 on {DATE} and whispered that {V.his} boyfriend was 'choking me.' column6: A charity's clothing donation bin was emptied by someone with a van on {DATE}, taking about $700 in donated clothing. The charity's camera showed {D}'s van. {DL} says {D.he} thought the bin was abandoned.
